16.2.d: द्यौस् ते \\ इति पृष्ठस्योपरि पाणिं धारयन्न् अनुपस्पृशन्न् उत्क्राम \\ इत्य् उत्क्रमयति ॥
16.2.m: Holding his hand above [the horse's] back without touching it, with 'dyaus te…', he makes it step off with 'utkrāma…'

16.2.s: udakramīt \\ ity abhimantrayate //
16.2.d: उदक्रमीत् \\ इत्य् अभिमन्त्रयते ॥
16.2.m: He addresses it with: 'udakramīt…'

16.2.s: āhavanīyavat sthāpayati piṇḍasya //
16.2.d: आहवनीयवत् स्थापयति पिण्डस्य ॥
16.2.m: He places [the horse] in the same position relative to the lump as [it was] relative to the Āhavanīya fire.

16.2.s: upaviśya mṛdam abhijuhoti \\ ā tvā jigharmi \\ iti vyatiṣaktābhyām ṛgbhyām āhutī sruveṇāśvapade //
16.2.d: उपविश्य मृदम् अभिजुहोति \\ आ त्वा जिघर्मि \\ इति व्यतिषक्ताभ्याम् ऋग्भ्याम् आहुती स्रुवेणाश्वपदे ॥
16.2.m: Sitting down, he offers oblations on the clay in the horse's footprint with the sruva, using the two intertwined verses beginning with: 'ā tvā jigharmi…'

16.2.s: abhryā piṇḍaṃ triḥ parilikhati pari vājapatir iti bahirbahir uttarayottarayābhryā piṇḍaṃ khanati devasya tvā \\ iti //
16.2.d: अभ्र्या पिण्डं त्रिः परिलिखति परि वाजपतिर् इति बहिर्बहिर् उत्तरयोत्तरयाभ्र्या पिण्डं खनति देवस्य त्वा \\ इति ॥
16.2.m: With the spade he draws three lines around the lump, each further outward with the following [mantra]: 'pari vājapatir…'; with the spade he digs out the lump with: 'devasya tvā…'

16.2.s: kṛṣṇājinam āstīryottaratas tasmin puṣkaraparṇam apāṃ pṛṣṭham iti //
16.2.d: कृष्णाजिनम् आस्तीर्योत्तरतस् तस्मिन् पुष्करपर्णम् अपां पृष्ठम् इति ॥
16.2.m: Having spread out a black antelope skin to the north, [he places] upon it a lotus leaf with: 'apāṃ pṛṣṭham…'

16.2.s: vimārṣṭy enad divas \\ iti //
16.2.d: विमार्ष्ट्य् एनद् दिवस् \\ इति ॥
16.2.m: He wipes it with: 'divas…'

16.2.s: ālabhata ubhe śarma ca sthas \\ iti //
16.2.d: आलभत उभे शर्म च स्थस् \\ इति ॥
16.2.m: He touches both with: 'śarma ca sthas…'

16.2.s: piṇḍam \\ purīṣyo 'si \\ iti //
16.2.d: पिण्डम् \\ पुरीष्यो ऽसि \\ इति ॥

16.2.s: pāṇibhyāṃ parigṛhṇāty enaṃ dakṣiṇottarābhyāṃ dakṣiṇaḥ sābhris tvām agne \\ iti ṣaḍbhiḥ sarvam̐ sakṛd dhṛtvā //
16.2.d: पाणिभ्यां परिगृह्णात्य् एनं दक्षिणोत्तराभ्यां दक्षिणः साभ्रिस् त्वाम् अग्ने \\ इति षड्भिः सर्वम्̐ सकृद् धृत्वा ॥
16.2.m: Standing to the south, he grasps it completely at once with both hands, the right over the left, together with the spade, with the six [verses] beginning with: 'tvām agne…'

16.3.s: puṣkaraparṇe nidadhāti //
16.3.d: पुष्करपर्णे निदधाति ॥
16.3.m: He places [the lump] down upon the lotus leaf.

16.3.s: apaḥ śvabhre 'vanayati \\ apo devīr iti //
16.3.d: अपः श्वभ्रे ऽवनयति \\ अपो देवीर् इति ॥
16.3.m: He pours water into the pit with: 'apo devīr…'

16.3.s: saṃ te \\ iti vā tam apakṣipati //
16.3.d: सं ते \\ इति वा तम् अपक्षिपति ॥
16.3.m: Or he throws it away with: 'saṃ te…'

16.3.s: anāmikayā saṃvapati purastāt paścād dakṣiṇata uttarataś ca //
16.3.d: अनामिकया संवपति पुरस्तात् पश्चाद् दक्षिणत उत्तरतश् च ॥
16.3.m: With the ring finger he scatters [soil] into [the pit] in the east, west, south, and north.

16.3.s: āstīrṇayor antān udgṛhṇāti sujātas \\ iti //
16.3.d: आस्तीर्णयोर् अन्तान् उद्गृह्णाति सुजातस् \\ इति ॥
16.3.m: He lifts up the ends of the two spread [coverings] with: 'sujātas…'

16.3.s: trivṛtā muñjayoktreṇopanahyati vāso agne \\ iti //
16.3.d: त्रिवृता मुञ्जयोक्त्रेणोपनह्यति वासो अग्ने \\ इति ॥
16.3.m: He ties them together with a triple cord of muñja grass with: 'vāso agne…'

16.3.s: uttiṣṭhati piṇḍam ādāya \\ ud u tiṣṭha \\ iti //
16.3.d: उत्तिष्ठति पिण्डम् आदाय \\ उद् उ तिष्ठ \\ इति ॥
16.3.m: Taking the lump, he stands up with: 'ud u tiṣṭha…'

16.3.s: ūrdhvabāhuḥ prāñcaṃ pragṛhṇāti \\ ūrdhva ū ṣu ṇas \\ iti //
16.3.d: ऊर्ध्वबाहुः प्राञ्चं प्रगृह्णाति \\ ऊर्ध्व ऊ षु णस् \\ इति ॥
16.3.m: With arms raised, he holds it forward toward the east with: 'ūrdhva ū ṣu ṇaḥ…'

16.3.s: avahṛtyoparinābhi dhārayann aśvaprabhṛtīn abhimantrayate sa jāta \ sthiro bhava \ śivo bhava \\ iti //
16.3.d: अवहृत्योपरिनाभि धारयन्न् अश्वप्रभृतीन् अभिमन्त्रयते स जात \ स्थिरो भव \ शिवो भव \\ इति ॥
16.3.m: Lowering it and holding it above the navel, he addresses [the animals] beginning with the horse with: 'sa jāta…', 'sthiro bhava…', and 'śivo bhava…'

16.3.s: dhārayaty eṣām upari piṇḍama nupaspṛśan praitu vājī \ vṛṣāgnim ity aśvakharayoḥ //
16.3.d: धारयत्य् एषाम् उपरि पिण्डम नुपस्पृशन् प्रैतु वाजी \ वृषाग्निम् इत्य् अश्वखरयोः ॥
16.3.m: He holds the lump above them without touching [them], with 'praitu vājī…' and 'vṛṣāgnim…' over the horse and the donkey.

16.3.s: agna āyāhi \\ ity āhṛtya kharāc chāgasya \\ ṛtam̐ satyam ity ā nidhānāt //
16.3.d: अग्न आयाहि \\ इत्य् आहृत्य खराच् छागस्य \\ ऋतम्̐ सत्यम् इत्य् आ निधानात् ॥
16.3.m: With 'agna āyāhi…', bringing [it] from the donkey, [he holds it] over the he-goat, [muttering] 'ṛtaṃ satyam…' until the putting down.

16.3.s: āyanty āvartya paśūn ajaḥ purastād rāsabho madhye //
16.3.d: आयन्त्य् आवर्त्य पशून् अजः पुरस्ताद् रासभो मध्ये ॥
16.3.m: They come forward, turning the animals around, with the he-goat in front and the donkey in the middle.

16.3.s: anaddhāpuruṣam īkṣate pūrvavad agniṃ purīṣyam iti //
16.3.d: अनद्धापुरुषम् ईक्षते पूर्ववद् अग्निं पुरीष्यम् इति ॥
16.3.m: He looks at a non-Aryan man, as before, with: 'agniṃ purīṣyam…'

16.3.s: uttarata āhavanīyasyoddhatāvokṣite sikatopakīrṇe parivṛte prāgdvāre piṇḍaṃ nidadhāti \\ oṣadhayas \\ iti //
16.3.d: उत्तरत आहवनीयस्योद्धतावोक्षिते सिकतोपकीर्णे परिवृते प्राग्द्वारे पिण्डं निदधाति \\ ओषधयस् \\ इति ॥
16.3.m: To the north of the Āhavanīya fire, on [ground that is] raised, sprinkled with water, strewn with sand, enclosed, and having an eastern entrance, he puts down the lump with: 'oṣadhayas…'

16.3.s: vi pājasā \\ iti pramucyainam ajalomāny ādāya prāgudīcaḥ paśūn utsṛjati //
16.3.d: वि पाजसा \\ इति प्रमुच्यैनम् अजलोमान्य् आदाय प्रागुदीचः पशून् उत्सृजति ॥
16.3.m: Untying it with 'vi pājasā…' and taking the goat hairs, he releases the animals toward the northeast.

16.3.s: āpo hi ṣṭhā \\ iti parṇakaṣāyapakvam udakam āsiñcati piṇḍe //
16.3.d: आपो हि ष्ठा \\ इति पर्णकषायपक्वम् उदकम् आसिञ्चति पिण्डे ॥
16.3.m: With 'āpo hi ṣṭhā…', he pours over the lump water boiled with a decoction of palāśa leaves.

16.3.s: phenaṃ ca tūṣṇīṃ tataḥ kṛtvā //
16.3.d: फेनं च तूष्णीं ततः कृत्वा ॥
16.3.m: And silently removing the froth from it;

16.3.s: ajalomabhiḥ sam̐sṛjati mitraḥ sam̐sṛjya \\ iti //
16.3.d: अजलोमभिः सम्̐सृजति मित्रः सम्̐सृज्य \\ इति ॥
16.3.m: He mixes [the clay] with the goat hairs with: 'mitraḥ saṃsṛjya…'

16.3.s: śarkarāyorasāśmacūrṇaiś ca rudrāḥ sam̐sṛjya \\ iti //
16.3.d: शर्करायोरसाश्मचूर्णैश् च रुद्राः सम्̐सृज्य \\ इति ॥
16.3.m: And with gravel, iron slag, and stone powder with: 'rudrāḥ saṃsṛjya…'

16.3.s: sam̐sṛṣṭām iti saṃyauti //
16.3.d: सम्̐सृष्टाम् इति संयौति ॥
16.3.m: He kneads it with: 'saṃsṛṣṭām…'

16.3.s: aṣāḍhāṃ karoti mahiṣī prathamavittā tadākhyā //
16.3.d: अषाढां करोति महिषी प्रथमवित्ता तदाख्या ॥
16.3.m: The chief queen, being the first-wedded wife, makes the aṣāḍhā brick, which is named after her.

16.3.s: yajamānapādamātrīṃ tryālikhitām //
16.3.d: यजमानपादमात्रीं त्र्यालिखिताम् ॥
16.3.m: It is of the size of the sacrificer's foot and marked with three lines.

16.3.s: yajamāna ukhāṃ karoti mṛdam ādāya makhasya śiras \\ iti //
16.3.d: यजमान उखां करोति मृदम् आदाय मखस्य शिरस् \\ इति ॥
16.3.m: Taking the clay with 'makhasya śiras…', the sacrificer makes the ukhā pot.

16.3.s: prādeśamātrīṃ tiryagūrdhvāṃ ca //
16.3.d: प्रादेशमात्रीं तिर्यगूर्ध्वां च ॥
16.3.m: It is a span wide and [a span] high.

16.3.s: pañcaprādeśām iṣumātrīṃ vā tiryakpañcapaśau //
16.3.d: पञ्चप्रादेशाम् इषुमात्रीं वा तिर्यक्पञ्चपशौ ॥
16.3.m: In a sacrifice with five animals, it is five spans or an arrow-length wide.

16.3.s: vasavas tvā \\ iti prathayati //
16.3.d: वसवस् त्वा \\ इति प्रथयति ॥
16.3.m: He broadens it out with: 'vasavas tvā…'

16.3.s: antān unnīya sarvataḥ prathamaṃ dhātum ādadhāti rudrās tvā \\ iti //
16.3.d: अन्तान् उन्नीय सर्वतः प्रथमं धातुम् आदधाति रुद्रास् त्वा \\ इति ॥
16.3.m: Raising up the edges all around, he lays the first layer with: 'rudrās tvā…'

16.3.s: saṃlipya ślakṣṇāṃ kṛtvottaram ādityās tvā \\ iti //
16.3.d: संलिप्य श्लक्ष्णां कृत्वोत्तरम् आदित्यास् त्वा \\ इति ॥
16.3.m: Smearing it together and making it smooth, [he lays] the upper one with: 'ādityās tvā…'

16.3.s: viśve tvā \\ iti samīkaroti //
16.3.d: विश्वे त्वा \\ इति समीकरोति ॥
16.3.m: He evens it with: 'viśve tvā…'

16.3.s: vitṛtīya uttare vartim̐ sarvataḥ karoti \\ adityai rāsnā \\ iti //
16.3.d: वितृतीय उत्तरे वर्तिम्̐ सर्वतः करोति \\ अदित्यै रास्ना \\ इति ॥
16.3.m: At the upper third [of the height], he makes a belt all around with: 'adityai rāsnā…'

16.3.s: ūrdhvās tūṣṇīṃ pratidiśaṃ catasro 'parā vartiṃ prāptāḥ //
16.3.d: ऊर्ध्वास् तूष्णीं प्रतिदिशं चतस्रो ऽपरा वर्तिं प्राप्ताः ॥
16.3.m: Silently [he makes] four other upright [bands], one in each direction, reaching to the belt.

16.4.m: He raises [projections] like breasts at their tops.
Some [prescribe that it has] two breasts or eight breasts.
He forms the rim with: 'aditiṣ ṭe…'

16.4.s: iṣṭakās tu tisro viśvajyotiṣaḥ pṛthaglakṣaṇās tryālikhitāḥ //
16.4.d: इष्टकास् तु तिस्रो विश्वज्योतिषः पृथग्लक्षणास् त्र्यालिखिताः ॥
16.4.m: There are, however, three viśvajyotis bricks, each with distinct marks and marked with three lines.
He sets aside extra clay.

16.4.s: saptabhir aśvaśakṛdbhir ukhāṃ dhūpayati dakṣiṇāgnyādīptair ekaikena vasavas tvā \\ iti pratimantram //
16.4.d: सप्तभिर् अश्वशकृद्भिर् उखां धूपयति दक्षिणाग्न्यादीप्तैर् एकैकेन वसवस् त्वा \\ इति प्रतिमन्त्रम् ॥
16.4.m: He fumigates the ukhā pot with seven horse-dung balls kindled from the Dakṣiṇāgni fire, one by one, with each respective mantra beginning with: 'vasavas tvā…'

16.4.s: abhryā śvabhraṃ caturaśraṃ khanati \\ aditiṣ ṭvā \\ iti //
16.4.d: अभ्र्या श्वभ्रं चतुरश्रं खनति \\ अदितिष् ट्वा \\ इति ॥
16.4.m: With the spade he digs a square pit with: 'aditiṣ ṭvā…'
Having spread fuel for baking, he places [the prepared objects] in it according to how they were made.
[He places] the ukhā pot upside down with: 'devānāṃ tvā…'
Having covered [them] with fuel for baking, he kindles [it] with fire from the Dakṣiṇāgni with: 'dhiṣaṇas tvā…'
Or the fumigation and baking [are done] with churned fire.
Looking [at it], he mutters: 'varūtrīṣ ṭvā…'
The burning and removal [of the ukhā pot] take place by day only.
He sets it right side up with: 'Unwavering...'

16.4.s: parigṛhya pātre karoti mitraitāṃ te \\ iti //
16.4.d: परिगृह्य पात्रे करोति मित्रैतां ते \\ इति ॥
16.4.m: Having seized it, he places it in a vessel with: 'O Mitra, this to you...'
He sprinkles it with goat's milk with each mantra: 'May the Vasus you...'
Of the [bricks] marked with three lines, beginning from the brick-making;
or [they are] marked with an indefinite number of lines on the next two.
The consecration [takes place] on the new-moon day, having sacrificed with the new-moon sacrifice.
There are [two cakes]: to Agni-Viṣṇu and to Agni Vaiśvānara.
There is a mess of cooked rice (caru) in clarified butter for the Ādityas.

16.4.s: prākṛtāny audgrabhaṇāni hutvā saptāgnikāni \\ ākūtim iti pratimantram //
16.4.d: प्राकृतान्य् औद्ग्रभणानि हुत्वा सप्ताग्निकानि \\ आकूतिम् इति प्रतिमन्त्रम् ॥
16.4.m: Having offered the archetypal elevation oblations (audgrabhaṇa), he offers seven oblations pertaining to the fire with each mantra: 'The intention...'

16.4.s: daṇḍochrayaṇāntaṃ kṛtvādhvaryuyajamānayor anyatara ukhām āhavanīye 'dhiśrayati muñjakulāyāvastīrṇām antare śaṇās \\ mā su bhitthās \\ iti tiṣṭhann udaṅ prāṅ //
16.4.d: दण्डोछ्रयणान्तं कृत्वाध्वर्युयजमानयोर् अन्यतर उखाम् आहवनीये ऽधिश्रयति मुञ्जकुलायावस्तीर्णाम् अन्तरे शणास् \\ मा सु भित्थास् \\ इति तिष्ठन्न् उदङ् प्राङ् ॥
16.4.m: Having performed [the rites] up to the erection of the staff, either the Adhvaryu or the sacrificer places the ukhā pot upon the Āhavanīya fire, lined with a nest of Muñja grass, with hemp fibers inside, standing facing northeast, with: 'Do not break...'
And during the fastening of the golden disc, the Viṣṇu-strides, and the Vātsapra chant.

16.4.s: agnāv ārūḍhe trayodaśāsyāṃ prādeśamātrīḥ samidha ādadhāti //
16.4.d: अग्नाव् आरूढे त्रयोदशास्यां प्रादेशमात्रीः समिध आदधाति ॥
16.4.m: When the fire has mounted [into the ukhā], he puts into it thirteen fuel sticks measuring a span (prādeśa).
Some say [he puts them in] without [the fire] having mounted, having poured embers into it.
[He puts in] a fuel stick of bamboo (kārmukī) anointed with clarified butter, with: 'Wood-fed...'
A fuel stick of Vikankata wood, with: 'Of the far...'
A fuel stick of Udumbara wood, with: 'Of the furthest...'
A fuel stick not cut with an axe, with: 'O Agni, what...'
A fuel stick lying on the ground, with: 'What eats...'
[He puts in eight] fuel sticks of Palāśa wood with each verse: 'Day by day...'
Wishing [the good] of a kṣatriya, [he uses] the next-to-last [verse].
The utterance of 'svāhā' applies to all [fuel sticks offered] into the ukhā.
Some [authorities place the rites] from the elevation oblations up to the staff at this point.

16.5.s: yajamānaḥ kaṇṭhe rukmaṃ pratimuñcate parimaṇḍalam ekavim̐śatipiṇḍaṃ kṛṣṇājinaniṣyūtaṃ lomasu śuklakṛṣṇeṣu śaṇasūtre trivṛty otam uparinābhi bahiṣpiṇḍam \\ dṛśāno rukmas \\ iti //
16.5.d: यजमानः कण्ठे रुक्मं प्रतिमुञ्चते परिमण्डलम् एकविम्̐शतिपिण्डं कृष्णाजिननिष्यूतं लोमसु शुक्लकृष्णेषु शणसूत्रे त्रिवृत्य् ओतम् उपरिनाभि बहिष्पिण्डम् \\ दृशानो रुक्मस् \\ इति ॥
16.5.m: The sacrificer fastens a golden disc around his neck, round, with twenty-one knobs, sewn to a black antelope skin with black and white hairs, threaded on a three-fold hemp cord, held above the navel, with the knobs facing outward, with: 'The golden disc seen...'
For the head-pads (iṇḍva), sling (śikya), and chair (āsandī), the ropes are made of Muñja grass, three-fold, smeared with clay.

16.5.s: parimaṇḍalābhyām iṇḍvābhyām ukhāṃ parigṛhṇāti naktoṣasā \\ iti //
16.5.d: परिमण्डलाभ्याम् इण्ड्वाभ्याम् उखां परिगृह्णाति नक्तोषसा \\ इति ॥
16.5.m: With two round pads he takes hold of the ukhā pot with: 'Night and dawn...'

16.5.s: āhavanīyasya purastād udgātrāsandīvad āsandyāṃ caturaśrāṅgyām̐ śikyavatyāṃ nidadhāti devā agnim iti //
16.5.d: आहवनीयस्य पुरस्ताद् उद्गात्रासन्दीवद् आसन्द्यां चतुरश्राङ्ग्याम्̐ शिक्यवत्यां निदधाति देवा अग्निम् इति ॥
16.5.m: To the east of the Āhavanīya, he places it on a four-legged chair equipped with a sling, like the chair for the Udgātṛ priest, with: 'The gods, Agni...'

16.5.s: śikyapāśaṃ pratimuñcate ṣaḍudyāmam \\ viśvā rūpāṇi \\ iti //
16.5.d: शिक्यपाशं प्रतिमुञ्चते षडुद्यामम् \\ विश्वा रूपाणि \\ इति ॥
16.5.m: He puts the loop of the sling over himself, [lifting it with] six pulls, with: 'All forms...'

16.5.s: saśikyaṃm prāñcaṃ pragṛhṇāti suparṇo 'si \\ iti piṇḍavat //
16.5.d: सशिक्यंम् प्राञ्चं प्रगृह्णाति सुपर्णो ऽसि \\ इति पिण्डवत् ॥
16.5.m: He lifts [the ukhā] along with the sling toward the east, with: 'You are the eagle...', as in the case of the lump [of clay].

Having consecrated [the brick] with this modification, some pile another layer: trough-piled (droṇacit), chariot-wheel-piled (rathacakracit), vulture-piled (kaṅkacit), triangle-piled (praugacit), double-triangle-piled (ubhayataḥprauga), or with heaped rubbish (samuhyapurīṣa).
In the case of the one with heaped rubbish, the bringing of the loose earth is done in every direction.

16.5.s: viṣṇukramān kramate viṣṇor iti pratimantram agnyudgrabhaṇaṃ ca tasmiṃstasmin //
16.5.d: विष्णुक्रमान् क्रमते विष्णोर् इति प्रतिमन्त्रम् अग्न्युद्ग्रभणं च तस्मिंस्तस्मिन् ॥
16.5.m: He steps the Viṣṇu-strides with each mantra: 'Of Viṣṇu...', and at each one there is the elevation of the fire.
He gazes at the quarters with: 'Stride along the quarters...'

16.5.s: piṇḍavat prāgudañcaṃ pragṛhṇāti \\ akrandad agnir iti //
16.5.d: पिण्डवत् प्रागुदञ्चं प्रगृह्णाति \\ अक्रन्दद् अग्निर् इति ॥
16.5.m: As in the case of the lump [of clay], he lifts it toward the northeast with: 'Agni has cried out...'
He brings it down with: 'O Agni, returning...'

16.5.s: uparinābhi dhārayan \\ ā tvāhārṣam ity abhimantrayate //
16.5.d: उपरिनाभि धारयन् \\ आ त्वाहार्षम् इत्य् अभिमन्त्रयते ॥
16.5.m: Holding it above the navel, he addresses it with: 'I have brought you...'

16.5.s: pāśā unmucya \\ ud uttamam iti piṇḍavat prāgdakṣiṇā pragṛhṇāti \\ agre brhan \\ iti //
16.5.d: पाशा उन्मुच्य \\ उद् उत्तमम् इति पिण्डवत् प्राग्दक्षिणा प्रगृह्णाति \\ अग्रे ब्र्हन् \\ इति ॥
16.5.m: Having loosened the loops, [reciting] 'The highest...', as in the case of the lump [of clay], he lifts it toward the southeast with: 'High at the start...'
He brings it down with: 'The swan seated in the clear...'
He places it on the chair with: 'The great...'

16.5.s: vātsapreṇa ca divas pari \\ ity ekādaśabhiḥ //
16.5.d: वात्सप्रेण च दिवस् परि \\ इत्य् एकादशभिः ॥
16.5.m: And with the Vātsapra hymn, with the eleven [verses beginning with]: 'From heaven at first...'
From this point on, there is repetition for a year.

16.6.m: At sunset, the pouring out of the ashes from the ukhā into a vessel takes place.

16.6.s: vācaṃ visṛjya samidādhānam \\ rātrīm̐rātrīm aprayāvam iti //
16.6.d: वाचं विसृज्य समिदाधानम् \\ रात्रीम्̐रात्रीम् अप्रयावम् इति ॥
16.6.m: Having released speech, [there is] the placing of the fuel stick with: 'Night after night, unceasing...'
Likewise at sunrise, the pouring out of ashes and so forth [take place].
And having placed the fuel stick at sunrise, the Viṣṇu-strides and the Vātsapra [take place] on alternate days.
[The rites] from the fastening of the golden disc up to the Vātsapra hymn are the Viṣṇu-strides.
Or [it is done] without conflicting with the Soma ritual, because of the predominance of that.

16.6.s: nyajya samidhaṃ vrate prattepratte \\ annapate \\ ity ādhānam //
16.6.d: न्यज्य समिधं व्रते प्रत्तेप्रत्ते \\ अन्नपते \\ इत्य् आधानम् ॥
16.6.m: Whenever the vrata drink is given, having dipped a piece of kindling into it, the laying on [of the kindling takes place] with: 'annapate…'
[This rule applies] to one who maintains [the fire in the pan] for a year, as well as to one who does not maintain it for a year.

16.6.s: prāg anaḥ kṛtvokhyasyottarataḥ samidādhānam \\ samidhāgnim iti //
16.6.d: प्राग् अनः कृत्वोख्यस्योत्तरतः समिदाधानम् \\ समिधाग्निम् इति ॥
16.6.m: Having turned the cart to face eastward, [he performs] the placing of fuel on the north side of the pan-fire with the mantra: "With fuel, the fire..."

16.6.s: sāsandīkam udyamya \\ ud u tvā \\ iti dakṣiṇato 'nasi karoti //
16.6.d: सासन्दीकम् उद्यम्य \\ उद् उ त्वा \\ इति दक्षिणतो ऽनसि करोति ॥
16.6.m: Lifting up [the pan] together with its chair, he places it on the cart toward the south with [the mantra]: "Up you..."
[He places] the Gārhapatya [fire] in an earthen pot toward the west.

16.6.s: anaḍvāhau yuktvā pred agne \\ iti prāṅ yātvā yathārtham //
16.6.d: अनड्वाहौ युक्त्वा प्रेद् अग्ने \\ इति प्राङ् यात्वा यथार्थम् ॥
16.6.m: Having yoked two draft-oxen, having driven eastwards with [the mantra]: "Forward, O Agni...", [he proceeds] as far as required.
He may mount [the cart] or he may walk by the side.

16.6.s: akṣe kharjati \\ akrandad agnir iti japati //
16.6.d: अक्षे खर्जति \\ अक्रन्दद् अग्निर् इति जपति ॥
16.6.m: When the axle creaks, he mutters: "Agni has cried out..."

16.6.s: vāse 'vaharaty uddhatāvokṣita uttarataḥ samidādhānam \\ prapra \\ iti //
16.6.d: वासे ऽवहरत्य् उद्धतावोक्षित उत्तरतः समिदाधानम् \\ प्रप्र \\ इति ॥
16.6.m: At the halting place, he unloads [the fires]; on [ground] dug up and sprinkled, on the north side, [he performs] the placing of fuel with [the mantra]: "Forward, forward..."
This is the driving around (vanīvāhana), whenever he desires during the consecrations (dīkṣās).
The casting of the ashes of the pan-fire into water takes place at the beginning of the purchase-rite [of soma],
subsequent to the driving around, according to the sequence.
[He casts the ashes into water] with a cup of palāśa leaf with one [verse]: "O divine waters..."
With the ring finger he takes [the ash] from what has been cast, having sunk [his hand], with [the mantra]: "Having sat..."
Throwing [it] back into the fire-pan, he attends upon [the fire] with [the mantra]: "Be mindful of me..."
Having touched [the fire] with a fuel-stick, [he performs] an expiation;

16.7.m: he offers clarified butter with [the mantra]: "To Viśvakarman..."
Having stood up, he puts on a fuel-stick with [the mantra]: "Thee back again..."
If the Gārhapatya fire goes out, having churned [fire afresh], [he rekindles it].
During the soma pressing days, having brought [fire] from the Āhavanīya fire by means of a glowing coal,
[he brings it] north of the Sadas to the Āgnīdhra fire.
And in all [such cases], [he performs] the expiation pertaining to the Soma sacrifice, each prior one according to its proper time.
If the fire-pan breaks, having placed a potsherd of the fire-pan inside a new pot with a wide mouth, he pours [the fire] into it.

16.7.s: ukhopaśaye piṣṭvā mṛdā sahokhāṃ karoty āvṛtā //
16.7.d: उखोपशये पिष्ट्वा मृदा सहोखां करोत्य् आवृता ॥
16.7.m: Having crushed the spare fire-pans together with clay, he makes a fire-pan according to the ritual procedure.
When it is baked, he pours [the fire] and the potsherd into it.
Having crushed the spare fire-pans and mixed [the powder with clay], he sets it aside.
Having sat down facing himself, [he performs] the piling [of bricks],
making his left arm inside, with bricks that have marks on their upper surface.

16.7.s: nitye sādanasūdadohasā upadhānād uttare tayā devatayā \ tā asya \\ iti //
16.7.d: नित्ये सादनसूददोहसा उपधानाद् उत्तरे तया देवतया \ ता अस्य \\ इति ॥
16.7.m: The setting [of the brick] and the Sūdadohas [formula] are constant; following the laying down [of the brick, he recites]: "By that deity..." and "Those of him..."
and because there is no prohibition handed down in the text.
In the case of [bricks] belonging to a single injunction and a single place, [the recitation is done] in common (tantra).

16.7.s: lokampṛṇāsu daśasudaśasu mantras \\ lokaṃ pṛṇa \\ iti //
16.7.d: लोकम्पृणासु दशसुदशसु मन्त्रस् \\ लोकं पृण \\ इति ॥
16.7.m: In the case of space-filling (lokampṛṇā) bricks, after every ten bricks the mantra: "Fill the space..." [is recited],
In each layer, having laid two [bricks],
[he lays] an odd group upon the spine (anūka);
The groups running from west to east face north;
No piling is done with broken or black [bricks].
On the last day of the consecrations, the measurement of the altar (vedi) and of the fire [takes place].
At the location of the pan-fire, he outlines the Gārhapatya [hearth] with half a fathom (vyāma).
Or stepping out takes place from the circular area of the Antaḥpātya peg.
The fire to be piled (citya) is one foot-measure behind the sacrificial post's hole.
By the sacrificer standing upright on tiptoe with arms raised, or standing flat-footed,

16.8.m: having measured a cord of two puruṣas,
and at half-puruṣa intervals on both sides.
[There is a mark] at one-fifth of a puruṣa from the middle [mark];

16.8.s: anupṛṣṭhyām āyamya pāśayoḥ śaṅkū madhye 'rdhapuruṣayoś ca //
16.8.d: अनुपृष्ठ्याम् आयम्य पाशयोः शङ्कू मध्ये ऽर्धपुरुषयोश् च ॥
16.8.m: Having stretched [the cord] along the spinal line (pṛṣṭhyā), [he drives] pegs into the two loops, at the middle, and at the two half-puruṣa marks.

16.8.s: pāśā unmucyārdhapuruṣīyayoḥ pratimucya dakṣiṇāyamya madhyame nitodaṃ karoti //
16.8.d: पाशा उन्मुच्यार्धपुरुषीययोः प्रतिमुच्य दक्षिणायम्य मध्यमे नितोदं करोति ॥
16.8.m: Having unfastened the loops and refastened them over the two [pegs] at the half-puruṣa marks, having stretched [the cord] to the south, he makes an incision at the middle.

16.8.s: unmucya pāśāv ekaṃ madhyame pratimucya dakṣṇādhinitodam āyamya madhyame śaṅkuḥ //
16.8.d: उन्मुच्य पाशाव् एकं मध्यमे प्रतिमुच्य दक्ष्णाधिनितोदम् आयम्य मध्यमे शङ्कुः ॥
16.8.m: Having unfastened the two loops and fastened one over the middle [peg], having stretched [it] to the south over the incision, a peg is [driven] at the middle.

16.8.s: tasmin pāśaṃ pratimucya pūrvārdhe ca dakṣiṇāyamya madhyame śaṅkuḥ //
16.8.d: तस्मिन् पाशं प्रतिमुच्य पूर्वार्धे च दक्षिणायम्य मध्यमे शङ्कुः ॥
16.8.m: Having fastened a loop over that [peg] and in the eastern half, having stretched [it] to the south, a peg is [driven] at the middle;

16.8.s: unmucya pūrvārdhyāt paścārdhe pratimucya dakṣiṇāyamya madhyame śaṅkuḥ //
16.8.d: उन्मुच्य पूर्वार्ध्यात् पश्चार्धे प्रतिमुच्य दक्षिणायम्य मध्यमे शङ्कुः ॥
16.8.m: Having unfastened [it] from the eastern half and fastened [it] in the western half, having stretched [it] to the south, a peg is [driven] at the middle;
and at the two half-puruṣa [points] on both sides.

16.8.s: dakṣiṇe pārśve pūrvavad āyamya pañcamabhāgīye śaṅkuḥ //
16.8.d: दक्षिणे पार्श्वे पूर्ववद् आयम्य पञ्चमभागीये शङ्कुः ॥
16.8.m: On the southern side, having stretched [the cord] as before, a peg is [driven] at the fifth-part [mark].

16.8.s: tamin pāśaṃ pratimucya pūrve cārdhapuruṣīye pañcamabhāgīyārdhapuruṣīyayoḥ saṃnipātya tasmiñ chaṅkuḥ //
16.8.d: तमिन् पाशं प्रतिमुच्य पूर्वे चार्धपुरुषीये पञ्चमभागीयार्धपुरुषीययोः संनिपात्य तस्मिञ् छङ्कुः ॥
16.8.m: Having fastened a loop over that [peg] and at the eastern half-puruṣa [peg], having brought together [the cords] at the fifth-part and half-puruṣa [pegs], a peg is [driven] at that [point of intersection].

16.8.s: ichan pakṣapuchāpyayeṣu caturaṅgulaṃcaturaṅgulam̐ saṃkarṣati vikarṣaty ante //
16.8.d: इछन् पक्षपुछाप्ययेषु चतुरङ्गुलंचतुरङ्गुलम्̐ संकर्षति विकर्षत्य् अन्ते ॥
16.8.m: If he wishes, at the junctions of the wings and the tail he draws in four aṅgulas each, [and] draws out [four aṅgulas each] at the end.

16.8.s: pañcārtniḥ puruṣo daśapado dvādaśāṅgulaṃ padaṃ prakramas tripadaḥ samavibhaktasya //
16.8.d: पञ्चार्त्निः पुरुषो दशपदो द्वादशाङ्गुलं पदं प्रक्रमस् त्रिपदः समविभक्तस्य ॥
16.8.m: A puruṣa is five aratnis [or] ten padas; a pada is twelve aṅgulas; a prakrama is three padas of [a puruṣa] divided equally.

16.8.s: paritatya rajjvā sahitaṃ bahīrajjvekaṣaṣṭe śate pariśrito minoti //
16.8.d: परितत्य रज्ज्वा सहितं बहीरज्ज्वेकषष्टे शते परिश्रितो मिनोति ॥
16.8.m: Having enclosed [the area] with a cord, together [with the space inside], outside the cord he fixes two hundred and sixty-one enclosing stones (pariśrit);
or three [times] ninety-four.
Pebbles are [placed] upright in the trench.
In the subsequent [layers or fires], [the enlargement is] simply by an increase of a puruṣa up to the one-hundred-and-one-fold.
The measurement of the altar (vedi) and bricks is according to the fire-altar.
[This rule applies] to the antaḥpātya peg and the Gārhapatya, if he wishes.

16.8.s: uttarapakṣasyāparasyām̐ sraktyāṃ pariśrito minoti jaṅghāmātrīṃ nābhimātrīṃ mukhamātrīm iti //
16.8.d: उत्तरपक्षस्यापरस्याम्̐ स्रक्त्यां परिश्रितो मिनोति जङ्घामात्रीं नाभिमात्रीं मुखमात्रीम् इति ॥
16.8.m: At the western corner of the northern wing, he fixes an enclosing stone [of height] measure of a shin, measure of the navel, or measure of the mouth.

17.1.m: On the next day, having performed [the rites] beginning with the carrying down [of the fire] up to the expiations, there is the combination of the Viṣṇukrama [steps] and the Vātsapra [hymn].
Having performed the Vātsapra [hymn], [the fire] is to be attended upon, if [he desires].

17.1.s: palāśaśākhayā gārhapatyaṃ vyudūhati \\ apeta vīta \\ iti pachaḥ pratidiśaṃ purastāt prathamam //
17.1.d: पलाशशाखया गार्हपत्यं व्युदूहति \\ अपेत वीत \\ इति पछः प्रतिदिशं पुरस्तात् प्रथमम् ॥
17.1.m: With a palāśa branch he sweeps away the Gārhapatya fire with [the formula] "Go away, depart..." quarter-verse by quarter-verse toward each direction, first in the east.

17.1.s: udīcīm̐ śākhām udasyoṣān nivapati saṃjñānam iti //
17.1.d: उदीचीम्̐ शाखाम् उदस्योषान् निवपति संज्ञानम् इति ॥
17.1.m: Having thrown the branch to the north, he scatters saline earth with [the formula] "Knowledge..."

17.1.s: sikatāś ca \\ agner bhasma \\ ity ūṣavat //
17.1.d: सिकताश् च \\ अग्नेर् भस्म \\ इत्य् ऊषवत् ॥
17.1.m: And sand with "The ashes of Agni...", like the saline earth.

17.1.s: pariśridbhiḥ pariśrayati pūrvavad ekavim̐śatyā cita stha \\ iti //
17.1.d: परिश्रिद्भिः परिश्रयति पूर्ववद् एकविम्̐शत्या चित स्थ \\ इति ॥
17.1.m: He encloses it with enclosing stones as before, twenty-one [in number], with "You are the layers..."

17.1.s: madhye 'rdhabṛhatīś catasro dakṣiṇottarāḥ prācīr upadadhāti dakṣiṇata udaṅṅ ayam̐ so agnir iti pratyṛcam //
17.1.d: मध्ये ऽर्धबृहतीश् चतस्रो दक्षिणोत्तराः प्राचीर् उपदधाति दक्षिणत उदङ्ङ् अयम्̐ सो अग्निर् इति प्रत्यृचम् ॥
17.1.m: In the middle, [moving] from south to north, facing east, he lays down four half-bṛhatī [bricks] from south [to north], facing north, verse by verse with "This Agni is he..."
Joined at the back, two [bricks] measuring a pāda, crosswise, and [two] at the east.

17.1.s: apareṇa parikramyaparikramya cayanam iḍām agne \\ iti paścime pratimantram uttarataḥ //
17.1.d: अपरेण परिक्रम्यपरिक्रम्य चयनम् इडाम् अग्ने \\ इति पश्चिमे प्रतिमन्त्रम् उत्तरतः ॥
17.1.m: Going round repeatedly by the west, the piling [is done with] "Agni, of Iḍā..." on the two western [bricks] with each respective mantra from the north;

17.1.s: cid asi \\ iti pūrve dakṣiṇataḥ pratimantram //
17.1.d: चिद् असि \\ इति पूर्वे दक्षिणतः प्रतिमन्त्रम् ॥
17.1.m: with "You are the layer..." on the two eastern [bricks] from the south with each respective mantra.
In the regular [rite, the formula is recited] for each brick on the crosswise ones.

17.1.s: tisṛṣu lokampṛṇāsu ca dvāyor vā daśasv ekasyāṃ ca //
17.1.d: तिसृषु लोकम्पृणासु च द्वायोर् वा दशस्व् एकस्यां च ॥
17.1.m: And on three Lokampṛṇā [bricks], or on two, on ten, and on one.

17.1.s: cātvāladeśāt purīṣaṃ nivapati \\ indraṃ viśvās \\ iti //
17.1.d: चात्वालदेशात् पुरीषं निवपति \\ इन्द्रं विश्वास् \\ इति ॥
17.1.m: From the site of the Cātvāla he scatters loose soil (purīṣa) with "Indra, all the..."
Having made [the layer] level to the brim, he pours out the contents of the ukhā [pot] with "Joined..."

17.1.s: sikatābhiḥ samambilāṃ kṛtvā māteva putram iti śikyād vimucyābhrivan nidhāyāsiñcati payo madhye tūṣṇīm //
17.1.d: सिकताभिः समम्बिलां कृत्वा मातेव पुत्रम् इति शिक्याद् विमुच्याभ्रिवन् निधायासिञ्चति पयो मध्ये तूष्णीम् ॥
17.1.m: Having made it level to the brim with sand, with "Like a mother a son...", having untied it from the sling and set it down like the spade, he pours milk silently into the middle.

17.1.s: nairṛtīḥ kṛṣṇās tuṣapakvās tisro 'lakṣaṇāḥ pādamātrīr haviṣyaśannahomavaddeśe dakṣiṇottarāḥ kṛtvā dakṣiṇāmukho 'nupaspṛśan //
17.1.d: नैरृतीः कृष्णास् तुषपक्वास् तिस्रो ऽलक्षणाः पादमात्रीर् हविष्यशन्नहोमवद्देशे दक्षिणोत्तराः कृत्वा दक्षिणामुखो ऽनुपस्पृशन् ॥
17.1.m: Three black [bricks] sacred to Nirṛti, baked with chaff, without marks, measuring a pāda, having arranged them from south to north in the place where the offerings of sacrificial food are made, facing south, without touching them with the hand;

17.2.m: [he lays them] turned away, verse by verse with "Him who does not press soma..."
He casts away the sling, the golden plate, the cord, the head-rest, and the chair beyond [the altar] with "Which to you..."

17.2.s: udapātraṃ niṣicyāntarātmeṣṭakam uttiṣṭhanti namo bhūtyai \\ iti //
17.2.d: उदपात्रं निषिच्यान्तरात्मेष्टकम् उत्तिष्ठन्ति नमो भूत्यै \\ इति ॥
17.2.m: Having poured out a water-vessel, they rise up between the self (trunk) and the bricks with "Homage to prosperity!"
Having approached without looking back, there is worship of the Śālādvārya [fire] with "Dwelling..."
At the conclusion of the haviṣkṛt call of the Prāyaṇīyā offering, he performs [the preparation] of the Mahāvedi beginning with the wooden sword (sphya) up to the touching [of the ground].
At the conclusion of the Prāyaṇīyā offering, he yokes a plough made of udumbara wood.
The rope is made of muñja grass and is threefold.
He yokes six, twelve, or twenty-four [oxen].

17.2.s: pūrveṇottarām̐saṃ dakṣiṇām agniśroṇim apareṇa tiṣṭhan yujyamānam abhimantrayate sīrā yuñjanti \\ iti //
17.2.d: पूर्वेणोत्तराम्̐सं दक्षिणाम् अग्निश्रोणिम् अपरेण तिष्ठन् युज्यमानम् अभिमन्त्रयते सीरा युञ्जन्ति \\ इति ॥
17.2.m: Standing to the east of the northern shoulder [and] south of the southern hip of the fire-altar, he addresses [the team] being yoked with "The ploughmen yoke the ploughs..."

17.2.s: ātmani kṛṣaty anupariśrichunam̐ suphālā iti pratyṛcam //
17.2.d: आत्मनि कृषत्य् अनुपरिश्रिछुनम्̐ सुफाला इति प्रत्यृचम् ॥
17.2.m: He ploughs on the trunk along the enclosing stones, verse by verse with "May the ploughshares [plough] auspiciously..."

17.3.m: kuśastambam upadadhāti madhye tūṣṇīm
pañcagṛhītenodgṛhṇann abhijuhoti sajūr abdas \\ iti

17.3.s: catasṛṣucatasṛṣu trīṃstrīn udacamasān ninayati yathākṛṣṭam audumbareṇa catuḥsraktinā //
17.3.d: चतसृषुचतसृषु त्रींस्त्रीन् उदचमसान् निनयति यथाकृष्टम् औदुम्बरेण चतुःस्रक्तिना ॥
17.3.m: catasṛṣucatasṛṣu trīṃstrīn udacamasān ninayati yathākṛṣṭam audumbareṇa catuḥsraktinā
tasmint sarvauṣadham āvapaty ekavarjam
abhojanaṃ tasyochvāsāt

17.3.s: yā oṣadhīr iti tricair vapaty udapātravat //
17.3.d: या ओषधीर् इति त्रिचैर् वपत्य् उदपात्रवत् ॥
17.3.m: yā oṣadhīr iti tricair vapaty udapātravat

17.3.d: सोमनिवपनाद्य् आतिथ्यहविष्कृतः कृत्वाहवनीयपरिश्रितो ऽभिमन्त्रयते चित स्थेति ॥
17.3.m: somanivapanādy ātithyahaviṣkṛtaḥ kṛtvāhavanīyapariśrito 'bhimantrayate cita stheti

17.3.s: lokeṣṭakā sphyenāhṛtya bahirveder anūkānteṣūpadadhāti tiṣṭhan mā mā him̐sīt \\ iti pratyṛcaṃ pratidiśaṃ purastāt prathamam //
17.3.d: लोकेष्टका स्फ्येनाहृत्य बहिर्वेदेर् अनूकान्तेषूपदधाति तिष्ठन् मा मा हिम्̐सीत् \\ इति प्रत्यृचं प्रतिदिशं पुरस्तात् प्रथमम् ॥
17.3.m: lokeṣṭakā sphyenāhṛtya bahirveder anūkānteṣūpadadhāti tiṣṭhan mā mā him̐sīt \\ iti pratyṛcaṃ pratidiśaṃ purastāt prathamam
uttarāparasyāḥ paścāt

17.3.s: uttarasyāḥ sikatāḥ pramārṣṭi jahāmi sedim iti //
17.3.d: उत्तरस्याः सिकताः प्रमार्ष्टि जहामि सेदिम् इति ॥
17.3.m: uttarasyāḥ sikatāḥ pramārṣṭi jahāmi sedim iti

17.3.s: uttaravediṃ nivapati catvārim̐śatpadāṃ yugamātrīṃ vā sarvataḥ kuśastambe //
17.3.d: उत्तरवेदिं निवपति चत्वारिम्̐शत्पदां युगमात्रीं वा सर्वतः कुशस्तम्बे ॥
17.3.m: uttaravediṃ nivapati catvārim̐śatpadāṃ yugamātrīṃ vā sarvataḥ kuśastambe

17.3.s: agne tava \\ iti sikatā nyupya chādayaty ātmānam //
17.3.d: अग्ने तव \\ इति सिकता न्युप्य छादयत्य् आत्मानम् ॥
17.3.m: agne tava \\ iti sikatā nyupya chādayaty ātmānam
āpyāyasva \\ iti sikatālambhanam ṛgbhyām

17.3.s: ātithyaśeṣādy opasadaḥ kṛtvā rohite carmaṇy ānaduhe 'ntaḥpātyapurastād iṣṭakāḥ karoti prathamaciteḥ //
17.3.d: आतिथ्यशेषाद्य् ओपसदः कृत्वा रोहिते चर्मण्य् आनदुहे ऽन्तःपात्यपुरस्ताद् इष्टकाः करोति प्रथमचितेः ॥
17.3.m: ātithyaśeṣādy opasadaḥ kṛtvā rohite carmaṇy ānaduhe 'ntaḥpātyapurastād iṣṭakāḥ karoti prathamaciteḥ
svayamātṛṇṇāḥ matyā ca

17.3.s: ājye nyajya kuśāgrāṇi tūṣṇīṃ prokṣati śvete 'śve purastāt tiṣṭhati śvetābhāve 'śvete śvābhāve 'naḍuhi //
17.3.d: आज्ये न्यज्य कुशाग्राणि तूष्णीं प्रोक्षति श्वेते ऽश्वे पुरस्तात् तिष्ठति श्वेताभावे ऽश्वेते श्वाभावे ऽनडुहि ॥
17.3.m: ājye nyajya kuśāgrāṇi tūṣṇīṃ prokṣati śvete 'śve purastāt tiṣṭhati śvetābhāve 'śvete śvābhāve 'naḍuhi
agnibhyaḥ prahriyamāṇebhyo 'nuvācayati

17.3.s: triruktāyām aśvapūrvāṃ citim̐ hṛtvā puchād dakṣiṇāṃ nidadhāti //
17.3.d: त्रिरुक्तायाम् अश्वपूर्वां चितिम्̐ हृत्वा पुछाद् दक्षिणां निदधाति ॥
17.3.m: triruktāyām aśvapūrvāṃ citim̐ hṛtvā puchād dakṣiṇāṃ nidadhāti
tīrthenāśvam ārohayaty uttarapakṣam apareṇa
anuyajuḥkṛṣṭaṃ pariṇayaty uttarataḥ prathamam

17.3.s: pratyañcam āgataṃ citim avaghrāpya pariṇīyotsṛjati paśuvat //
17.3.d: प्रत्यञ्चम् आगतं चितिम् अवघ्राप्य परिणीयोत्सृजति पशुवत् ॥
17.3.m: pratyañcam āgataṃ citim avaghrāpya pariṇīyotsṛjati paśuvat

17.3.s: uttaravediprokṣaṇādy ā sambhāranivapanāt kṛtvottaravedim apareṇa tiṣṭhan yajamānas \\ mayi gṛhṇāmi \\ iti japati //
17.3.d: उत्तरवेदिप्रोक्षणाद्य् आ सम्भारनिवपनात् कृत्वोत्तरवेदिम् अपरेण तिष्ठन् यजमानस् \\ मयि गृह्णामि \\ इति जपति ॥
17.3.m: uttaravediprokṣaṇādy ā sambhāranivapanāt kṛtvottaravedim apareṇa tiṣṭhan yajamānas \\ mayi gṛhṇāmi \\ iti japati

17.4.s: uttānaṃ prāñcam̐ hiraṇyapuruṣaṃ tasmin hiraṇyagarbhas \\ iti //
17.4.d: उत्तानं प्राञ्चम्̐ हिरण्यपुरुषं तस्मिन् हिरण्यगर्भस् \\ इति ॥
17.4.m: uttānaṃ prāñcam̐ hiraṇyapuruṣaṃ tasmin hiraṇyagarbhas \\ iti

17.4.s: upaviśya pañcagṛhītaṃ juhoti puruṣe kṛṇuṣva pājas \\ iti pratyṛcaṃ pratidiśaṃ parisarpam //
17.4.d: उपविश्य पञ्चगृहीतं जुहोति पुरुषे कृणुष्व पाजस् \\ इति प्रत्यृचं प्रतिदिशं परिसर्पम् ॥
17.4.m: upaviśya pañcagṛhītaṃ juhoti puruṣe kṛṇuṣva pājas \\ iti pratyṛcaṃ pratidiśaṃ parisarpam

17.4.s: kārṣmaryamayīṃ dakṣiṇataḥ pāṇimātrapuṣkarāṃ bāhumātrīm pādamātrīṃ vā sāmarthyāt ghṛtapūrṇām agneṣ ṭvā \\ iti //
17.4.d: कार्ष्मर्यमयीं दक्षिणतः पाणिमात्रपुष्करां बाहुमात्रीम् पादमात्रीं वा सामर्थ्यात् घृतपूर्णाम् अग्नेष् ट्वा \\ इति ॥
17.4.m: kārṣmaryamayīṃ dakṣiṇataḥ pāṇimātrapuṣkarāṃ bāhumātrīm pādamātrīṃ vā sāmarthyāt ghṛtapūrṇām agneṣ ṭvā \\ iti

17.4.s: evam audumbarīm uttarato dadhipūrṇām indrasya tvā \\ iti //
17.4.d: एवम् औदुम्बरीम् उत्तरतो दधिपूर्णाम् इन्द्रस्य त्वा \\ इति ॥
17.4.m: evam audumbarīm uttarato dadhipūrṇām indrasya tvā \\ iti

17.4.s: svayamātṛṇṇāṃ puruṣe śarkarāṃ chidrām \\ dhruvāsi \\ iti //
17.4.d: स्वयमातृण्णां पुरुषे शर्करां छिद्राम् \\ ध्रुवासि \\ इति ॥
17.4.m: svayamātṛṇṇāṃ puruṣe śarkarāṃ chidrām \\ dhruvāsi \\ iti

17.4.s: mūlāgravatīṃ dūrvāṃ tasyāṃ purastād bhūmiprāptām \\ kāṇḍātkāṇḍāt \\ iti //
17.4.d: मूलाग्रवतीं दूर्वां तस्यां पुरस्ताद् भूमिप्राप्ताम् \\ काण्डात्काण्डात् \\ इति ॥
17.4.m: mūlāgravatīṃ dūrvāṃ tasyāṃ purastād bhūmiprāptām \\ kāṇḍātkāṇḍāt \\ iti

17.4.s: ṛtavye madhuś ca mādhavaś ca \\ iti //
17.4.d: ऋतव्ये मधुश् च माधवश् च \\ इति ॥
17.4.m: The two seasonal bricks (ṛtavyā) [are laid] with [the mantra]: "Madhu and Mādhava..."
He makes marks on the cord for the Svayamātṛṇṇā, Retaḥsic, Viśvajyotis, Ṛtavyā, and Aṣāḍhā [bricks] for the purpose of [determining their] positions.

17.4.s: kūrmaṃ dadhimadhughṛtair anakti madhu vātās \\ iti //
17.4.d: कूर्मं दधिमधुघृतैर् अनक्ति मधु वातास् \\ इति ॥
17.4.m: He anoints the tortoise with curd, honey, and clarified butter, with [the mantra]: 'The winds [blow] sweet…'.

17.4.d: अरत्निमात्रे ऽषाढां दक्षिणेमावकासूपरिष्टाच् च पुरुषम् अभिमुखम् ॥
17.4.m: At a cubit's distance south of the Aṣāḍhā brick, on [a bed of] avakā plants, and above [with avakā plants], [he places] it facing the man [brick/effigy].

17.5.m: With three [mantras beginning with]: 'In the depth of the waters…'.

17.5.s: ulūkhalamusale svayamātṛṇṇām uttareṇāratnimātre audumbare prādeśamātre caturaśram ulūkhalaṃ madhyasaṃgṛhītam ūrdhvam vṛttaṃ musalaṃ dakṣiṇam ulūkhalāt \\ viṣṇoḥ karmāṇi \\ iti //
17.5.d: उलूखलमुसले स्वयमातृण्णाम् उत्तरेणारत्निमात्रे औदुम्बरे प्रादेशमात्रे चतुरश्रम् उलूखलं मध्यसंगृहीतम् ऊर्ध्वम् वृत्तं मुसलं दक्षिणम् उलूखलात् \\ विष्णोः कर्माणि \\ इति ॥
17.5.m: [He places] a mortar and pestle made of udumbara wood, a span in size, the mortar being four-cornered, constricted in the middle, and upright, and the pestle being round, south of the mortar, a cubit north of the Svayamātṛṇṇā [brick], with [the mantra]: '[These are] the deeds of Viṣṇu'.

17.5.s: ulūkhala ukhāṃ kṛtvopaśayāṃ piṣṭvā nyupya purastāt \\ dhruvāsi \\ ity ukhām //
17.5.d: उलूखल उखां कृत्वोपशयां पिष्ट्वा न्युप्य पुरस्तात् \\ ध्रुवासि \\ इत्य् उखाम् ॥
17.5.m: Having placed the fire-pan (ukhā) upon the mortar, pounded the [wild grain called] upaśayā, and poured [it] into the eastern part [of the pan], [he places] the fire-pan with [the mantra]: 'Firm are you'.

17.5.s: agne yukṣvā hi \\ iti pratyṛcam̐ sruvāhutī juhoty ukhāyām //
17.5.d: अग्ने युक्ष्वा हि \\ इति प्रत्यृचम्̐ स्रुवाहुती जुहोत्य् उखायाम् ॥
17.5.m: With each verse [beginning with]: 'O Agni, yoke indeed…', he offers sruva-oblations into the fire-pan.
Or [there is only] reverent attendance (upasthāna) for one who has borne [the fire in the fire-pan] for a full year.

17.5.s: pratiśiraḥ saptasapta hiraṇyaśakalān mukhe karoti samyak sravanti \\ iti //
17.5.d: प्रतिशिरः सप्तसप्त हिरण्यशकलान् मुखे करोति सम्यक् स्रवन्ति \\ इति ॥
17.5.m: For each head [of the five victims], he puts seven chips of gold into the mouth with [the mantra]: 'Flowing together…'.
Into the two ears with: 'This has become…'.
Some [authorities hold that he puts] all [chips] even into a single one [i.e., only into the human head].
Having taken up the human head with [the mantra]: 'Giver of thousands…', [he deposits it] in the middle.
[The heads] of the horse and of the ram to the north, [placed] east and west [respectively].
With the respective mantras beginning with: 'The sun, the embryo…', according to the sequence of the mantras.

17.5.s: citraṃ devānām ity ardharcaśaḥ sruvāhutī madhyame //
17.5.d: चित्रं देवानाम् इत्य् अर्धर्चशः स्रुवाहुती मध्यमे ॥
17.5.m: With half-verses [beginning with]: 'The wondrous face of the gods…', he offers two sruva-oblations upon the middle [head, namely the human head].

17.5.s: bahirvedy udaṅ tiṣṭhann upatiṣṭhata utsargair imaṃ mā him̐sīr iti pratimantram //
17.5.d: बहिर्वेद्य् उदङ् तिष्ठन्न् उपतिष्ठत उत्सर्गैर् इमं मा हिम्̐सीर् इति प्रतिमन्त्रम् ॥
17.5.m: Standing outside the vedi facing north, he reverently attends [them] with release-mantras (utsargas), verse by verse, [beginning with]: 'Do not harm this one…'.
Or [he reverently attends] each one after each placement according to the characteristic mark [in the mantra].
Some [say he recites] all the mantras even over a single [head, i.e., the human head].
Shifting the mantras of placement, one finger-breadth on the head that has spread widest.

17.6.s: etya ca tvaṃ yaviṣṭha \\ iti cityopasthānam //
17.6.d: एत्य च त्वं यविष्ठ \\ इति चित्योपस्थानम् ॥
17.6.m: Having approached, [he performs] reverent attendance of the layer with: 'And you, O youngest…'.

17.6.s: apareṇa svayamātṛṇṇām etyāpasyāḥ pañcapañcānūkānteṣu \\ apāṃ tveman \\ iti pratimantram //
17.6.d: अपरेण स्वयमातृण्णाम् एत्यापस्याः पञ्चपञ्चानूकान्तेषु \\ अपां त्वेमन् \\ इति प्रतिमन्त्रम् ॥
17.6.m: Having gone to the west of the Svayamātṛṇṇā brick, [he places] the Apasyā bricks, five each at the ends of the spine, with the respective mantras: 'In the pathway of the waters, you…'.

17.6.s: vyāghāraṇavat prāṇabhṛtaḥ karṇasahitā daśadaśa puruṣam upārpyaike retaḥsigvelāyāṃ ca sarvato yathāyogam ayaṃ puras \\ iti pratimantram //
17.6.d: व्याघारणवत् प्राणभृतः कर्णसहिता दशदश पुरुषम् उपार्प्यैके रेतःसिग्वेलायां च सर्वतो यथायोगम् अयं पुरस् \\ इति प्रतिमन्त्रम् ॥
17.6.m: As in the case of the anointing, [he places] the Prāṇabhṛt bricks, along with the corner ones, ten by ten, some [teachers say] bringing them close to the human effigy, and along the mark of the Retaḥsic bricks on all sides as appropriate, with the respective mantra: 'This one in front…'.
The second [set of ten with]: 'This one behind…'.

17.6.s: lokampṛṇā dakṣiṇām̐sād adhy ā madhyāt pradakṣiṇam ānūkāntāt pūrvasmāt //
17.6.d: लोकम्पृणा दक्षिणाम्̐साद् अध्य् आ मध्यात् प्रदक्षिणम् आनूकान्तात् पूर्वस्मात् ॥
17.6.m: [He places] the Lokampṛṇā bricks starting from the right shoulder up to the middle, sunwise, up to the eastern end of the spine.
[He fills in] the wings and the tail with bricks directed outward, starting from the joints.
In the middle he scatters loose earth as before.
He covers the eastern half of the spine.

17.7.s: citiṃ purīṣavatīm upatiṣṭhate vārtrahatyāya \\ iti saptabhiḥ //
17.7.d: चितिं पुरीषवतीम् उपतिष्ठते वार्त्रहत्याय \\ इति सप्तभिः ॥
17.7.m: He reverently attends the layer covered with loose earth with the seven [verses beginning with]: 'For the slaying of Vṛtra…'.
Some [say] with eight, or with ten.
During the Upasads, between the forenoon and afternoon [services, take place] the piling and the scattering of loose earth.

17.7.s: trir aśvaṃ pariṇīyopāstamayaṃ paśuvad utsṛjya tāvat pratiparyeti //
17.7.d: त्रिर् अश्वं परिणीयोपास्तमयं पशुवद् उत्सृज्य तावत् प्रतिपर्येति ॥
17.7.m: Having led the horse around three times, [and] having released it near sunset like an animal [victim], he walks around [the altar] in reverse order that many times.
The leading around continues until the placing of the fire.
In a sacrifice with three Upasads: two [layers] on the first [day], three on the middle [day].
In a sacrifice with twelve Upasads, [there is] an alternation of layer and loose earth.
In a sacrifice with four months of Upasads, [the work proceeds] in periods of twelve days.
In a [sacrifice with] a year [of Upasads, it proceeds] in periods of thirty-six days each.
In the Tāpaścita sacrifice, [there are] month by month the layer and the loose earth for the four [layers].
In the fifth [layer], the Asapatnā and Virāj bricks [are placed] on the first day.
[The bricks] beginning with Nākapat for a month.
On the last two days, [the bricks] beginning with the Vikarṇī on the former [day].
The first [layer contains] two thousand space-filler [bricks], minus fifty.
Of the marked [bricks], [they are laid] to the south and north, [and] in the middle of the others.
Or the third [layer contains] thirty-six hundred, [and] the others eighteen hundred.
The space-filler [bricks] of the Gārhapatya [hearth are laid] in the first [layer].
In the first and last [layers], foot-long [bricks are added as] extras.
Breaking those exceeding multiples of ten, he should place [them] on the rubbish heap.

17.8.m: In the second [layer, he places] the Āśvinī bricks in each direction.
At the line of the Retaḥsic bricks, north of the spine [of the altar], the eastern [Āśvinī brick is placed] in the second [space].
The fifth one north of the southern [brick].
Likewise, next to the Vaiśvadevī bricks, [he places] the Prāṇabhṛt bricks.
The fifth [bricks] of all [these sets are placed] as before.
[He places] the Āśvinī bricks, [each] with its respective mantra, beginning with: 'Firm dwelling...'

17.8.s: śukraś ca śuciś ca \\ ity ṛtavye pūrvayor upari //
17.8.d: शुक्रश् च शुचिश् च \\ इत्य् ऋतव्ये पूर्वयोर् उपरि ॥
17.8.m: With: 'Śukra and Śuci...', [he places] two seasonal bricks on top of the eastern two [bricks];
[He places] the Vaiśvadevī bricks, [each] with its respective mantra, beginning with: 'In union with the seasons...'
The Prāṇabhṛt bricks with [the mantras beginning with]: 'My breath...'

17.8.s: vayasyāḥ pañcapañcānūkānteṣu mūrdhā vayas \\ iti pratimantram catasraḥ purastāt //
17.8.d: वयस्याः पञ्चपञ्चानूकान्तेषु मूर्धा वयस् \\ इति प्रतिमन्त्रम् चतस्रः पुरस्तात् ॥
17.8.m: The Vayasyā bricks, five each at the ends of the spine, with their respective mantras, beginning with: 'The head is vigor...', [first] four to the east,
[then four] to the south, to the north, [and] to the west.
Beginning from the southern buttock, the space-filler bricks [are laid] as before.

17.9.m: In the third [layer, he places] the naturally perforated brick in the middle with: 'Indra and Agni...'

17.9.s: anūkeṣu pañca diśyā vaiśvadevīvat \\ rājñy asi \\ iti pratimantram //
17.9.d: अनूकेषु पञ्च दिश्या वैश्वदेवीवत् \\ राज्ञ्य् असि \\ इति प्रतिमन्त्रम् ॥
17.9.m: On the spinal axes, five directional bricks, like the Vaiśvadevī bricks, [each] with its respective mantra: 'You are the queen...'
With: 'Viśvakarman...', [he places] the all-light brick on top of the eastern [naturally perforated brick];

17.9.s: ṛtavye nabhaś ca nabhasyaś ca \\ iti //
17.9.d: ऋतव्ये नभश् च नभस्यश् च \\ इति ॥
17.9.m: Two seasonal bricks with: 'Nabhas and Nabhasya...'
Two western [seasonal bricks] with: 'Iṣ and Ūrj...'

17.9.s: pūrvārdhe prāṇabhṛto daśa \\ āyur me \\ iti pratimantram //
17.9.d: पूर्वार्धे प्राणभृतो दश \\ आयुर् मे \\ इति प्रतिमन्त्रम् ॥
17.9.m: In the eastern half, ten Prāṇabhṛt bricks, [each] with its respective mantra: 'My life...'

17.9.s: chandasyā dvādaśadvādaśāpyeṣu mā chandas \\ iti pratimantram //
17.9.d: छन्दस्या द्वादशद्वादशाप्येषु मा छन्दस् \\ इति प्रतिमन्त्रम् ॥
17.9.m: The metre bricks, twelve by twelve on each side, [each] with its respective mantra: 'Mā metre...'
having left space for the Vālakhilyā bricks in the west.
Seven Vālakhilyā bricks in the east;
or to the west of the Prāṇabhṛt bricks;
[He places them] each with its respective mantra: 'You are the head, the ruler...'
Beginning from the northern buttock, the space-filler bricks [are laid] as before.

17.10.m: In the fourth [layer], at the ends of the spinal axes, two each to the south and north;
west of the eastern two, fourteen [bricks];
According to some, [some are placed] in the southeastern intermediate region;
or north of the southern two.
[He places] the northern [brick] of the eastern two with: 'Swift, the threefold...';
the southern [brick] of the western two with: 'The supporter, the twenty-onefold...';
the southern [brick] of the southern two with: 'Shining, the fifteenfold...';
the southern [brick] of the northern two with: 'The sky, the seventeenfold...'
fourteen [bricks], each with its own mantra, beginning with 'Speed, the eighteenth...'.
[He places] the southern of the two eastern ones with 'Agni's share...'.
[He places] the northern of the two western ones with 'Mitra's share...'.
[He places] the northern of the two southern ones with 'The share of the men-watchers...'.
[He places] the northern of the two northern ones with 'Indra's share...'.
six [bricks], each with its own mantra, beginning with 'The Vasus' share...'.

17.10.s: ṛtavye sahaś ca sahasyaś ca \\ iti //
17.10.d: ऋतव्ये सहश् च सहस्यश् च \\ इति ॥
17.10.m: [He places] two seasonal [bricks] with 'Sahas and Sahasya...'.

17.10.s: retaḥsigvelāyāṃ ca saptadaśa sarvato nava dakṣiṇenānūkam̐ sṛṣṭīr ekayāstuvata \\ iti pratimantram //
17.10.d: रेतःसिग्वेलायां च सप्तदश सर्वतो नव दक्षिणेनानूकम्̐ सृष्टीर् एकयास्तुवत \\ इति प्रतिमन्त्रम् ॥
17.10.m: And in the line of the Retaḥsic [bricks], seventeen on all sides, nine to the south of the spine: [these] Sṛṣṭi [bricks], each with its own mantra, beginning with 'With the one they praised...'.
From the northern shoulder onwards, [he places] Lokampṛṇā [bricks] as before.

17.11.m: In the fifth [layer], at the ends, like the Āśvinī [bricks, he places] the Asapatnā [bricks].
Between the two southern ones there is the distance of a cubit.
Each with its own mantra: 'Agni, the born...'.

17.11.s: virājo daśadaśa pratidiśaṃ purastāt prathamam evaś chandas \\ iti pratimantram //
17.11.d: विराजो दशदश प्रतिदिशं पुरस्तात् प्रथमम् एवश् छन्दस् \\ इति प्रतिमन्त्रम् ॥
17.11.m: Ten Virāj [bricks] in each direction, first in the east, each with its own mantra: 'Eva is metre...'.
The Gāyatrī [brick is] an Asapatnā [brick], because inside the group it is impossible.
Or having placed half-foot [bricks] west of the Uṣṇih [bricks].
Touching the Asapatnā [bricks], the others are inside.

17.11.s: sarvato 'ṣāḍhāvelāyām̐ stomabhāgās \\ raśminā satyāya \\ iti pratimantram //
17.11.d: सर्वतो ऽषाढावेलायाम्̐ स्तोमभागास् \\ रश्मिना सत्याय \\ इति प्रतिमन्त्रम् ॥
17.11.m: All around in the line of the Aṣāḍhā [brick, he places] the Stomabhāgā [bricks], each with its own mantra: 'By the ray for truth...'.
Fifteen to the south of the spine.

17.11.s: veṣaśrīḥ kṣatrāya kṣatraṃ jinva \\ iti trim̐śattamīm eke //
17.11.d: वेषश्रीः क्षत्राय क्षत्रं जिन्व \\ इति त्रिम्̐शत्तमीम् एके ॥
17.11.m: Some [place] the thirtieth [brick with] 'Veṣaśrīḥ, enliven the ruling power for the ruling power!'.

17.11.s: purīṣam āsvāvapati mantreṇa vā tāpaś citasya tūṣṇīm̐śruteḥ //
17.11.d: पुरीषम् आस्वावपति मन्त्रेण वा तापश् चितस्य तूष्णीम्̐श्रुतेः ॥
17.11.m: He pours loose soil onto them with a mantra, or silently on account of the scriptural statement regarding the Tāpaścita [sacrifice].

17.12.s: nākasado 'nūkeṣu pūrvavarjam ṛtavyāvelāyām āśvinīvat \\ rājñy asi \\ iti pratimantram //
17.12.d: नाकसदो ऽनूकेषु पूर्ववर्जम् ऋतव्यावेलायाम् आश्विनीवत् \\ राज्ञ्य् असि \\ इति प्रतिमन्त्रम् ॥
17.12.m: [He places] the Nākasad [bricks] along the spines, except the eastern one, in the line of the seasonal [bricks], like the Āśvinī [bricks], each with its own mantra: 'You are queen...'.

17.12.s: purīṣam opyopari \\ ayaṃ puras \\ iti pañcacūḍāḥ pratimantram //
17.12.d: पुरीषम् ओप्योपरि \\ अयं पुरस् \\ इति पञ्चचूडाः प्रतिमन्त्रम् ॥
17.12.m: Having poured loose soil above, [he places] the Pañcacūḍā [bricks], each with its own mantra: 'This in front...'.

17.12.s: pratidiśaṃ yathāliṅgam //
17.12.d: प्रतिदिशं यथालिङ्गम् ॥
17.12.m: In each direction according to the characteristic mark.

17.12.s: paścimottamā //
17.12.d: पश्चिमोत्तमा ॥

17.12.s: chandasyās tisrastisro 'nūkānteṣu purastād gāyatrīr agnir mūrdhā \\ iti pratyṛcam //
17.12.d: छन्दस्यास् तिस्रस्तिस्रो ऽनूकान्तेषु पुरस्ताद् गायत्रीर् अग्निर् मूर्धा \\ इति प्रत्यृचम् ॥
17.12.m: Three Chandasyā [bricks] at each of the spine-ends; in the east, the Gāyatrī [bricks], verse by verse: 'Agni is head...'.

17.12.s: uttarāś ca //
17.12.d: उत्तराश् च ॥

17.12.s: purastāt triṣṭubho retaḥsigvelāyām \\ bhuvo yajñasya \\ iti //
17.12.d: पुरस्तात् त्रिष्टुभो रेतःसिग्वेलायाम् \\ भुवो यज्ञस्य \\ इति ॥
17.12.m: In the east, [he places] the Triṣṭubh [bricks] in the line of the Retaḥsic [bricks] with 'The world of the sacrifice...'.

17.12.s: jagatīś ca paścād ayam iha \\ iti //
17.12.d: जगतीश् च पश्चाद् अयम् इह \\ इति ॥
17.12.m: And the Jagatī [bricks] in the west with 'This one here...'.

17.12.s: aparās tābhyo 'nuṣṭubhaḥ sakhāyaḥ saṃ vas \\ iti //
17.12.d: अपरास् ताभ्यो ऽनुष्टुभः सखायः सं वस् \\ इति ॥
17.12.m: West of those, the Anuṣṭubh [bricks] with 'Companions, together for you...'.

17.12.s: aṣāḍhāvelāyāḥ purastād bṛhatīr enā vas \\ iti //
17.12.d: अषाढावेलायाः पुरस्ताद् बृहतीर् एना वस् \\ इति ॥
17.12.m: East of the line of the Aṣāḍhā [brick, he places] the Bṛhatī [bricks] with 'With this for you...'.

17.12.s: bhadro nas \\ iti kakubhas tābhyo bṛhatyantaraśruter mantrakrameṇa //
17.12.d: भद्रो नस् \\ इति ककुभस् ताभ्यो बृहत्यन्तरश्रुतेर् मन्त्रक्रमेण ॥
17.12.m: With 'Auspicious to us...', the Kakubh [bricks] [are placed] next to them, because of the scriptural mention of [their placement] between the Bṛhatī [bricks], according to the sequence of the mantras.

17.12.s: uddhṛtāny apakṛṣyechan //
17.12.d: उद्धृतान्य् अपकृष्येछन् ॥
17.12.m: He desires [to place them] having drawn out and shifted back [the others].

17.12.s: aparā gāyatrībhya uṣṇihas \\ agne vājasya \\ iti //
17.12.d: अपरा गायत्रीभ्य उष्णिहस् \\ अग्ने वाजस्य \\ इति ॥
17.12.m: West of the Gāyatrī [bricks], the Uṣṇih [bricks] with 'O Agni, of vigour...'.

17.12.s: anūkānte dakṣiṇe paṅktīr agniṃ tam iti //
17.12.d: अनूकान्ते दक्षिणे पङ्क्तीर् अग्निं तम् इति ॥
17.12.m: At the southern spine-end, the Paṅkti [bricks] with 'That Agni...'.

17.12.s: uttare padapaṅktīr agne tam adya \\ iti //
17.12.d: उत्तरे पदपङ्क्तीर् अग्ने तम् अद्य \\ इति ॥
17.12.m: At the northern, the Padapaṅkti [bricks] with 'Agni, him today...'.

17.12.s: purīṣavatyāḥ pūrvām atichandasaṃ prācyau purīṣasahite bhadrā rātir vṛtratūrye 'vasthirā \\ agnim̐ hotāram iti //
17.12.d: पुरीषवत्याः पूर्वाम् अतिछन्दसं प्राच्यौ पुरीषसहिते भद्रा रातिर् वृत्रतूर्ये ऽवस्थिरा \\ अग्निम्̐ होतारम् इति ॥
17.12.m: East of the one having loose soil, [he places] the Atichandas [brick], both facing east, accompanied by loose soil, with 'Auspicious gift, in the contest against Vṛtra...', 'Firm...', 'Agni, the Hotṛ priest...'.

17.12.s: agne tvam ity anūkānte 'pare dvipadāḥ //
17.12.d: अग्ने त्वम् इत्य् अनूकान्ते ऽपरे द्विपदाः ॥
17.12.m: With 'Agni, you...', the Dvipadā [bricks] at the western spine-end.

17.12.s: madhye 'ṣṭeṣṭakaṃ gārhapatyam //
17.12.d: मध्ये ऽष्टेष्टकं गार्हपत्यम् ॥
17.12.m: In the middle, [he builds] the Gārhapatya consisting of eight bricks.

17.12.s: punaścitiṃ copari tadvad yena ṛṣayas \\ iti pratyṛcam //
17.12.d: पुनश्चितिं चोपरि तद्वद् येन ऋषयस् \\ इति प्रत्यृचम् ॥
17.12.m: And above, in the same way, the Punaściti, verse by verse: 'Whereby the ṛṣis...'.

17.12.s: puchasaṃdhāv eke //
17.12.d: पुछसंधाव् एके ॥

17.12.s: pūrvārdhe vā //
17.12.d: पूर्वार्धे वा ॥

17.12.s: gārhapatyaṃ puchasaṃdhau kṛtvā //
17.12.d: गार्हपत्यं पुछसंधौ कृत्वा ॥
17.12.m: Having built the Gārhapatya at the junction of the tail,

17.12.s: ṛtavye tapaś ca tapasyaś ca \\ iti //
17.12.d: ऋतव्ये तपश् च तपस्यश् च \\ इति ॥
17.12.m: [he places] two seasonal [bricks] with 'Tapas and Tapasya...'.

17.12.s: viśvajyotiṣam \\ parameṣṭhī tvā \\ iti //
17.12.d: विश्वज्योतिषम् \\ परमेष्ठी त्वा \\ इति ॥
17.12.m: [He places] the Viśvajyotis [brick] with 'Parameṣṭhin [established] you...'.

17.12.s: dakṣiṇām̐sāt pratyag aratnimātrād adhi lokampṛṇāḥ pūrvavat //
17.12.d: दक्षिणाम्̐सात् प्रत्यग् अरत्निमात्राद् अधि लोकम्पृणाः पूर्ववत् ॥
17.12.m: From the southern shoulder onwards, one cubit to the west, [he places] the Lokampṛṇā [bricks] as before.

17.12.s: prachādya purīṣeṇa vikarṇīsvayamātṛṇṇe śarkare sam̐spṛṣṭe chidre prothad aśvas \\ ity uttarāṃ vikarṇīm āyoṣ ṭvā \\ iti svayamātṛṇṇām //
17.12.d: प्रछाद्य पुरीषेण विकर्णीस्वयमातृण्णे शर्करे सम्̐स्पृष्टे छिद्रे प्रोथद् अश्वस् \\ इत्य् उत्तरां विकर्णीम् आयोष् ट्वा \\ इति स्वयमातृण्णाम् ॥
17.12.m: Having covered [it] with loose soil, two gravel pieces—the Vikarṇī and the Svayamātṛṇṇā—are touched, perforated; with 'Snorting, the horse...', [he places] the northern Vikarṇī; with 'Ayu [has fashioned] you...', the Svayamātṛṇṇā.

17.12.s: sakṛn nitye //
17.12.d: सकृन् नित्ये ॥

17.12.s: puruṣābhihomavat tiṣṭhann agniṃ prokṣati hiraṇyaśakalasahasreṇa śate dvedve prakirati sahasrasya \\ iti pratimantram //
17.12.d: पुरुषाभिहोमवत् तिष्ठन्न् अग्निं प्रोक्षति हिरण्यशकलसहस्रेण शते द्वेद्वे प्रकिरति सहस्रस्य \\ इति प्रतिमन्त्रम् ॥
17.12.m: Standing as in the offering over the Puruṣa, he sprinkles the fire-altar with a thousand chips of gold; he scatters two on each hundred, each with its own mantra: 'Of the thousand...'.

18.1.s: śatarudriyahoma uttarapakṣasyāparasyām̐ sraktyāṃ pariśritsvarkaparṇenārkakāṣṭhena śātayant saṃtataṃ jartilamiśrān gavedhukāsaktūn ajākṣīram eke tiṣṭhann udaṅ namas te \\ ity adhyāyena //
18.1.d: शतरुद्रियहोम उत्तरपक्षस्यापरस्याम्̐ स्रक्त्यां परिश्रित्स्वर्कपर्णेनार्ककाष्ठेन शातयन्त् संततं जर्तिलमिश्रान् गवेधुकासक्तून् अजाक्षीरम् एके तिष्ठन्न् उदङ् नमस् ते \\ इत्य् अध्यायेन ॥
18.1.m: The Śatarudriya offering [takes place] on the western corner of the northern wing, on the enclosing stones; with an Arka leaf [and] an Arka stick, letting drop a continuous stream of crushed Gavedhukā seeds mixed with wild sesamum—some say goat's milk—standing and facing north, with the chapter beginning 'Homage to you...'.
At the end of three anuvākas [there is] the utterance of 'svāhā' at the level of the knees.
And at the end of five, at the level of the navel.
And before the descending verses, at the level of the mouth.

18.1.s: pratilomaṃ pratyavarohān juhoti pramāṇeṣu namo 'stu \\ iti pratimantram //
18.1.d: प्रतिलोमं प्रत्यवरोहान् जुहोति प्रमाणेषु नमो ऽस्तु \\ इति प्रतिमन्त्रम् ॥
18.1.m: He offers the descending verses in reverse order at the [respective] heights, each with its own mantra: 'Homage be...'.
He throws the two offering implements into the Cātvāla pit.

18.2.s: cityaṃ pariṣiñcaty agnīd dakṣiṇe nikakṣe 'driṃ kṛtvā \\ aśmann ūrjam ity adrer adhi //
18.2.d: चित्यं परिषिञ्चत्य् अग्नीद् दक्षिणे निकक्षे ऽद्रिं कृत्वा \\ अश्मन्न् ऊर्जम् इत्य् अद्रेर् अधि ॥
18.2.m: The Agnīdh priest pours around the altar-fire; placing a stone in the right armpit, [he pours] from above the stone with 'O stone, sap!...'.

18.2.s: aśmaṃs te kṣut \\ ity adrau kumbhaṃ kṛtvā mayi ta ūrg ity ādāyaivaṃ dvir aparam //
18.2.d: अश्मंस् ते क्षुत् \\ इत्य् अद्रौ कुम्भं कृत्वा मयि त ऊर्ग् इत्य् आदायैवं द्विर् अपरम् ॥
18.2.m: With 'O stone, your hunger...', having placed the jar on the stone, taking it up with 'In me is your sap...', he does the same twice further.

18.2.s: kumbhe 'driṃ kṛtvā dakṣiṇasyāṃ vediśroṇau prāṅ tiṣṭhan dakṣiṇāsyati yaṃ dviṣmas \\ iti //
18.2.d: कुम्भे ऽद्रिं कृत्वा दक्षिणस्यां वेदिश्रोणौ प्राङ् तिष्ठन् दक्षिणास्यति यं द्विष्मस् \\ इति ॥
18.2.m: Having placed the stone in the jar, standing facing east on the southern hip of the altar, he throws it towards the south with 'Whom we hate...'.
If it is unbroken, he should tell [someone] to break it.
The breaking is upon the jar, because of capability.

18.2.s: anapekṣam etyodaṅ prāṅ tiṣṭhann ātmana upari prāpaṇānte japati \\ imā me \\ iti //
18.2.d: अनपेक्षम् एत्योदङ् प्राङ् तिष्ठन्न् आत्मन उपरि प्रापणान्ते जपति \\ इमा मे \\ इति ॥
18.2.m: Having approached without looking back, standing facing north-east, at the conclusion of bringing [the water] over himself, he mutters: "These my…"

18.2.s: maṇḍūkāvakāvetasaśākhā veṇau baddhvāvakarṣati mantrakṛṣṭavat samudrasya tvā \\ iti pratyṛcam //
18.2.d: मण्डूकावकावेतसशाखा वेणौ बद्ध्वावकर्षति मन्त्रकृष्टवत् समुद्रस्य त्वा \\ इति प्रत्यृचम् ॥
18.2.m: Having tied a frog, avakā plants, and a cane branch to a bamboo stick, he drags it along, as if drawing lines with mantras, with each verse of: "Thee of the ocean…"

18.2.s: pakṣapuchāni cābhyātmam agne pāvaka rociṣā \\ iti //
18.2.d: पक्षपुछानि चाभ्यात्मम् अग्ने पावक रोचिषा \\ इति ॥
18.2.m: and towards the body over the wings and tail with: "O Agni, purifying with splendour…"

18.2.s: veṇum utkare kṛtvā cityam ālabhya tiṣṭhan //
18.2.d: वेणुम् उत्करे कृत्वा चित्यम् आलभ्य तिष्ठन् ॥
18.2.m: Having placed the bamboo stick on the rubbish heap, standing while touching the fire altar,

18.3.s: hiṅkṛtya sāma gāyati //
18.3.d: हिङ्कृत्य साम गायति ॥

18.3.s: purastād gāyatram //
18.3.d: पुरस्ताद् गायत्रम् ॥

18.3.s: dakṣiṇe pakṣe rathantaram uttare bṛhad ātmani vāmadevyaṃ puche yajñāyajñiyaṃ dakṣiṇe nikakṣe prajāpatihṛdayam agnyuktham̐ śam̐sa \\ ity āha //
18.3.d: दक्षिणे पक्षे रथन्तरम् उत्तरे बृहद् आत्मनि वामदेव्यं पुछे यज्ञायज्ञियं दक्षिणे निकक्षे प्रजापतिहृदयम् अग्न्युक्थम्̐ शम्̐स \\ इत्य् आह ॥
18.3.m: on the right wing, the Rathantara; on the left, the Bṛhat; on the body, the Vāmadevya; on the tail, the Yajñāyajñiya; on the right armpit, the Prajāpatihṛdaya; and he says: "Recite the Agnyuktha."

18.3.s: aupavasathye visṛṣṭavāci pañcagṛhīte hiraṇyaśakalān prāsyati pañca //
18.3.d: औपवसथ्ये विसृष्टवाचि पञ्चगृहीते हिरण्यशकलान् प्रास्यति पञ्च ॥
18.3.m: On the preparation day (aupavasathya), when speech is released, he casts five chips of gold into five ladlings [of ghee].

18.3.s: dadhimadhughṛtaṃ pātryām̐ samāsicya sthālyāṃ vā mahāmukhyāṃ kuśamuṣṭiṃ copary ubhayam ādāya cityārohaṇam \\ namas te \\ iti //
18.3.d: दधिमधुघृतं पात्र्याम्̐ समासिच्य स्थाल्यां वा महामुख्यां कुशमुष्टिं चोपर्य् उभयम् आदाय चित्यारोहणम् \\ नमस् ते \\ इति ॥
18.3.m: Having poured together curds, honey, and ghee into a dish or into a pot with a wide mouth, and taken both along with a handful of kuśa grass upon them, ascending the fire altar [is performed] with: "Homage to thee…"

18.3.s: svayamātṛṇṇāyāṃ pañcagṛhītaṃ juhoti nābhivad dhiraṇyādarśanaṃ ca nṛṣade veṭ \\ iti pratimantram //
18.3.d: स्वयमातृण्णायां पञ्चगृहीतं जुहोति नाभिवद् धिरण्यादर्शनं च नृषदे वेट् \\ इति प्रतिमन्त्रम् ॥
18.3.m: He offers the five ladlings upon the naturally perforated brick (svayamātṛṇṇā) as upon the navel, and without the gold being seen, with each mantra: "To the one seated among men, veṭ…"

18.3.s: samāsiktān kuśaiḥ prokṣati sapariśritkaṃ bāhyena ca ye devās \\ iti //
18.3.d: समासिक्तान् कुशैः प्रोक्षति सपरिश्रित्कं बाह्येन च ये देवास् \\ इति ॥
18.3.m: With the kuśa grass, he sprinkles the mingled liquids together with the enclosing stones, and also outside, with: "Which gods…"

18.3.s: prāṇadās \\ ity avarohati //
18.3.d: प्राणदास् \\ इत्य् अवरोहति ॥
18.3.m: He steps down with: "Giver of breath…"

18.3.s: evam ārohaṇāvarohaṇam ataḥ //
18.3.d: एवम् आरोहणावरोहणम् अतः ॥
18.3.m: Thus [is] the ascending and descending from now on.

18.3.s: upasadante pravargyotsādanaṃ yathoktam agnau pariṣyande vā //
18.3.d: उपसदन्ते प्रवर्ग्योत्सादनं यथोक्तम् अग्नौ परिष्यन्दे वा ॥
18.3.m: At the end of the Upasad, the disposal of the Pravargya takes place as prescribed, either on the fire or on the overflowing stream.

18.3.s: svayamātṛṇṇāspṛṣṭaṃ prathamam //
18.3.d: स्वयमातृण्णास्पृष्टं प्रथमम् ॥
18.3.m: The first [brick] touched is the naturally perforated brick.

18.3.s: pañcagṛhītaṃ juhoti \\ agnis tigmena \\ ity ṛcā ṣoḍaśagṛhītārdham anuvākaśeṣeṇa //
18.3.d: पञ्चगृहीतं जुहोति \\ अग्निस् तिग्मेन \\ इत्य् ऋचा षोडशगृहीतार्धम् अनुवाकशेषेण ॥
18.3.m: He offers the five ladlings with the verse: "Agni with sharp…", and half of the sixteen ladlings with the rest of the anuvāka;

18.3.s: cakṣuṣaḥ pitā \\ ity anuvākenāṣṭābhir ṛgbhiḥ sarvāṇi caitāni śālāgnau juhoti //
18.3.d: चक्षुषः पिता \\ इत्य् अनुवाकेनाष्टाभिर् ऋग्भिः सर्वाणि चैतानि शालाग्नौ जुहोति ॥
18.3.m: and with the anuvāka: "Father of the eye…", with eight verses. And all these he offers into the hall-fire (śālāgni).

18.3.s: ārdraudumbarīr ghṛtoṣitās tisras \\ ud enam ity ādadhāti pratyṛcam //
18.3.d: आर्द्रौदुम्बरीर् घृतोषितास् तिस्रस् \\ उद् एनम् इत्य् आदधाति प्रत्यृचम् ॥
18.3.m: He places three moist udumbara sticks soaked in ghee, one with each verse of: "Upwards him…"

18.3.s: agniṃ praṇayati //
18.3.d: अग्निं प्रणयति ॥

18.3.s: preṣyati \\ udyachedhmam \ upayachopayamanīḥ //
18.3.d: प्रेष्यति \\ उद्यछेध्मम् \ उपयछोपयमनीः ॥
18.3.m: He gives the call: "Lift up the fuel bundle; take hold of the under-supports;

18.3.s: agnaye prahriyamāṇāyānubrūhi \\ agnīd ekasphyayānūdehi \ brahmann apratirathaṃ japa \\ iti //
18.3.d: अग्नये प्रह्रियमाणायानुब्रूहि \\ अग्नीद् एकस्फ्ययानूदेहि \ ब्रह्मन्न् अप्रतिरथं जप \\ इति ॥
18.3.m: recite for the fire being carried forward; O Agnīdh, follow behind with a single sphya; O Brahman, mutter the Apratiratha hymn."

18.3.s: triruktāyām udyamya \\ ud u tvā \\ iti cityaṃ gachanti pañca diśas \\ iti //
18.3.d: त्रिरुक्तायाम् उद्यम्य \\ उद् उ त्वा \\ इति चित्यं गछन्ति पञ्च दिशस् \\ इति ॥
18.3.m: When [the verse] has been recited three times, having lifted it up with: "Upwards thee…", they go to the fire altar with: "The five quarters…"

18.3.s: āgnīdhradeśād dakṣiṇaṃ pṛṣṭhyāsahitaṃ pṛśnyaśmānam upadadhāti vimānas \\ iti //
18.3.d: आग्नीध्रदेशाद् दक्षिणं पृष्ठ्यासहितं पृश्न्यश्मानम् उपदधाति विमानस् \\ इति ॥
18.3.m: South of the Āgnīdhra place, along the spine-line (pṛṣṭhyā), he sets down a variegated stone with: "The measurer…"

18.3.s: na nitye //
18.3.d: न नित्ये ॥

18.3.s: nidhāyainam atikrāmanti \\ indraṃ viśvās \\ iti //
18.3.d: निधायैनम् अतिक्रामन्ति \\ इन्द्रं विश्वास् \\ इति ॥
18.3.m: Having laid it down, they step across it with: "Indra, all…"

18.4.m: They ascend the fire altar with: "Stride forth with the fire…"

18.4.s: svayamātṛṇṇām adhy agniṃ dhārayañ chuklavatsāpayasābhijuhoti kṛṣṇāyā dohanena svayamātṛṇṇām avasiñcan naktoṣāsā \\ iti //
18.4.d: स्वयमातृण्णाम् अध्य् अग्निं धारयञ् छुक्लवत्सापयसाभिजुहोति कृष्णाया दोहनेन स्वयमातृण्णाम् अवसिञ्चन् नक्तोषासा \\ इति ॥
18.4.m: Holding the fire above the naturally perforated brick, he offers milk from [a cow] with a white calf, pouring it down upon the naturally perforated brick with the milk of a black cow, with: "Night and Dawn…"
Here some [prescribe] the [mantras] beginning with the paitudārava wood.

18.4.s: tasyām agniṃ nidadhāti suparṇo 'si \\ iti vaṣaṭkāreṇa //
18.4.d: तस्याम् अग्निं निदधाति सुपर्णो ऽसि \\ इति वषट्कारेण ॥
18.4.m: He places the fire upon it with: "A fine-winged bird art thou…", accompanied by the vaṣaṭ-call;

18.4.s: samidādhānam̐ śāmīlīvaikaṅkatyaudumbaryas tām̐ savitur iti pratyṛcam uttamā sakarṇakā //
18.4.d: समिदाधानम्̐ शामीलीवैकङ्कत्यौदुम्बर्यस् ताम्̐ सवितुर् इति प्रत्यृचम् उत्तमा सकर्णका ॥
18.4.m: The placing of fuel sticks: śamī, kārṣmarya, vikaṅkata, and udumbara sticks, with each verse of: "That of Savitṛ…"; the last one has ear-like sprouts.
In the absence of ear-like sprouts, they are smeared with curd drops.

18.4.s: sruvāhutī juhoti \\ agne tam adya \\ iti ca pratyṛcam //
18.4.d: स्रुवाहुती जुहोति \\ अग्ने तम् अद्य \\ इति च प्रत्यृचम् ॥
18.4.m: He offers dipping-spoon oblations with each verse of: "O Agni, him today…",
and the full-spoon oblation (pūrṇāhuti) with: "Seven are thy…"
Standing, [he places] the fuel sticks everywhere in the middle;
having sat down, [he offers] the oblations at the ends.
Here [takes place] the attendance upon the fifth [layer] with seven verses, because of the laying down of everything;
or after having piled the dhiṣṇya hearths, because of connection with the highest.
If he wishes, he may touch it with: "The year art thou…"
He apportions the offerings to Vaiśvānara and the Maruts as prescribed.
Having set the Vaiśvānara [cake] on the fire, [he sets] the two Māruta [cakes] to the south and north,
and to the west, closer together;

18.4.s: puchād aparān kuśān āstīryāhavanīyasahitān vā tatrāsādanam //
18.4.d: पुछाद् अपरान् कुशान् आस्तीर्याहवनीयसहितान् वा तत्रासादनम् ॥
18.4.m: Having spread kuśa grass to the west of the tail, or together with the Āhavanīya fire, the setting down takes place there.

18.4.s: vaiśvānareṇa pracarya sarvahutena hastena mārutān juhoty upaviśya vaiśvānare vā vaiśvānaraṃ pṛthuṃ kṛtvā śukrajyotir iti pratimantram //
18.4.d: वैश्वानरेण प्रचर्य सर्वहुतेन हस्तेन मारुतान् जुहोत्य् उपविश्य वैश्वानरे वा वैश्वानरं पृथुं कृत्वा शुक्रज्योतिर् इति प्रतिमन्त्रम् ॥
18.4.m: Having performed the rite with the Vaiśvānara [cake] as entirely offered, having sat down, he offers the Māruta [cakes] with his hand into the Vaiśvānara [fire], or having made the Vaiśvānara [fire] wide, with each mantra: "Of bright light…"
The Āraṇyānūcya [rite] [takes place] without the vimukha mantra.
He mutters: "Indra, the divine…"
Or he makes [the sacrificer] recite: "This breast…"

18.5.s: vasordhārāṃ juhoty audumbaryā pañcagṛhītam̐ saṃtataṃ yajamāno 'raṇye 'nūcye 'gniprāpte vājaś ca me \\ ity aṣṭānuvākena //
18.5.d: वसोर्धारां जुहोत्य् औदुम्बर्या पञ्चगृहीतम्̐ संततं यजमानो ऽरण्ये ऽनूच्ये ऽग्निप्राप्ते वाजश् च मे \\ इत्य् अष्टानुवाकेन ॥
18.5.m: The sacrificer offers the continuous shower of wealth (vasordhārā) with the udumbara ladle, consisting of five ladlings, when the Āraṇyānūcya has reached the fire, with the eight anuvākas: "And strength for me…"

18.5.s: agnaye svāhā \\ iti ṣaṭ pārthāni juhoti //
18.5.d: अग्नये स्वाहा \\ इति षट् पार्थानि जुहोति ॥
18.5.m: He offers the six Pārtha offerings with: "To Agni, svāhā…"

18.5.s: vājaprasavīyāni vaprāvat sambhṛtya camasavat sruveṇa vājapeyikāni vājasyemam iti //
18.5.d: वाजप्रसवीयानि वप्रावत् सम्भृत्य चमसवत् स्रुवेण वाजपेयिकानि वाजस्येमम् इति ॥
18.5.m: Having gathered the Vājaprasavīya oblations as at the mound, [and offered them] with the dipping spoon like the cups, the Vājapeya oblations [are offered] with: "This of vigour…",
and the offerings pertaining to Agni with: "Now of vigour…"

18.5.s: sruvaṃ prāsya pariśritspṛkkṛṣṇājinam āstīrya puchād uttaram̐ śeṣe 'paḥ kṛtvā //
18.5.d: स्रुवं प्रास्य परिश्रित्स्पृक्कृष्णाजिनम् आस्तीर्य पुछाद् उत्तरम्̐ शेषे ऽपः कृत्वा ॥
18.5.m: Throwing down the dipping spoon, spreading a black antelope skin touching the enclosing stones to the north of the tail [of the altar], and putting water into the residue;
Or milk and water, according to the Vedic text: "They belong to the Vājapeya";

18.5.s: tatrābhiṣicyate brahmavarcasakāmaś cityanvārabdhas \\ devasya tvā \\ iti //
18.5.d: तत्राभिषिच्यते ब्रह्मवर्चसकामश् चित्यन्वारब्धस् \\ देवस्य त्वा \\ इति ॥
18.5.m: There one desiring spiritual lustre is sprinkled, touching the altar, with [the mantra]: "At the impulse of the divine [Savitṛ]...";
On a he-goat skin, if he desires nourishment;
Some [say it takes place] to the south of the altar, or on it;

18.5.s: prāsya camasam indrāya svāhā \\ iti ṣaḍ juhoti pratimantram //
18.5.d: प्रास्य चमसम् इन्द्राय स्वाहा \\ इति षड् जुहोति प्रतिमन्त्रम् ॥
18.5.m: Having thrown down the cup, he offers six [oblations] with: "To Indra svāhā!", per mantra;

18.5.s: dvādaśagṛhītaṃ vigrāhaṃ juhoti \\ ṛtāṣāḍ iti pratisvāhākāram̐ rāṣṭrabhṛto vāṭkārāntaḥ pūrvaḥpūrvo mantraḥ //
18.5.d: द्वादशगृहीतं विग्राहं जुहोति \\ ऋताषाड् इति प्रतिस्वाहाकारम्̐ राष्ट्रभृतो वाट्कारान्तः पूर्वःपूर्वो मन्त्रः ॥
18.5.m: He makes a twelve-fold drawing and offers [it] with each svāhā-call [in]: "Ṛtāṣāḍ..."; or the realm-sustaining [oblations]—each preceding mantra ends with a vāṭ-call;

18.5.s: pañcagṛhītaṃ ca rathaśirasy adhyadhy āhavanīyaṃ dhriyamāṇe pañcakṛtvaḥ sa no bhuvanasya \\ iti //
18.5.d: पञ्चगृहीतं च रथशिरस्य् अध्यध्य् आहवनीयं ध्रियमाणे पञ्चकृत्वः स नो भुवनस्य \\ इति ॥
18.5.m: And five-times-drawn [clarified butter], while the chariot-head is held right over the Āhavanīya fire, five times with: "May he of the world...";
The carrying around the chariot seat is sunwise;
The Adhvaryu priest faces the chariot-head;

18.6.s: vātahomān juhoty añjalināhṛtya purastād bahirveder adho dakṣiṇasyāṃ dhury uttarata uttarasyāṃ dakṣiṇato dakṣiṇāpraṣṭeḥ samudro 'si \\ iti pratimantram //
18.6.d: वातहोमान् जुहोत्य् अञ्जलिनाहृत्य पुरस्ताद् बहिर्वेदेर् अधो दक्षिणस्यां धुर्य् उत्तरत उत्तरस्यां दक्षिणतो दक्षिणाप्रष्टेः समुद्रो ऽसि \\ इति प्रतिमन्त्रम् ॥
18.6.m: Having taken [water] in the hollow of his hands, he offers the wind-oblations in front, outside the sacrificial altar, below the southern yoke, to the north on the northern [yoke], to the south of the right-hand outrigger horse, per mantra with: "You are the ocean...";
And the leading around of the yoke-halter [takes place] everywhere;
Having taken [the chariot], it is carried to the Adhvaryu's dwelling;
At the time of the sacrificial gifts, he gives [it] to the Adhvaryu priest;

18.6.s: nava juhoti yās te \\ iti pratimantram //
18.6.d: नव जुहोति यास् ते \\ इति प्रतिमन्त्रम् ॥
18.6.m: He offers nine [oblations] with: "Those which are yours...", per mantra;
Knowing [them], he may alternatively offer those stated in the Brāhmaṇa;

18.6.s: havirdhānaprakṣālanādy āgnīdhrālambhanāt kṛtvā dhiṣṇyāṃś cinoty aṣṭeṣṭakāṃ lokampṛṇābhiś catuḥsraktīṃs tiraśco nyupyanyupya //
18.6.d: हविर्धानप्रक्षालनाद्य् आग्नीध्रालम्भनात् कृत्वा धिष्ण्यांश् चिनोत्य् अष्टेष्टकां लोकम्पृणाभिश् चतुःस्रक्तींस् तिरश्चो न्युप्यन्युप्य ॥
18.6.m: Having performed [the rites] from the washing of the havirdhāna carts up to the touching of the Āgnīdhra hearth, he piles the dhiṣṇya hearths with eight bricks [each], four-cornered, scattering [earth] crosswise repeatedly with the lokampṛṇā bricks;
And a speckled stone on the Āgnīdhra hearth;
On the Hotṛ's hearth, three times with twenty-one [bricks];
On the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin's hearth, twice with eleven; six on the Mārjālīya hearth;
Having placed the enclosing stones around according to the number of bricks;
[The rites] from the assignments up to the cake-sviṣṭakṛt are like those of the consecration ceremony;

18.6.s: agniyojanaṃ prātaranuvākam upākariṣyan paridhīn ālambhya yathāpūrvam agniṃ yunajmi \\ iti pratyṛcam //
18.6.d: अग्नियोजनं प्रातरनुवाकम् उपाकरिष्यन् परिधीन् आलम्भ्य यथापूर्वम् अग्निं युनज्मि \\ इति प्रत्यृचम् ॥
18.6.m: The yoking of the fire: when about to inaugurate the morning recitation, touching the enclosing sticks in regular sequence, [he yokes it] with: "I yoke Agni...", per verse;

18.6.s: āgnimārutastotrapurastād vimocanaṃ paridhiṣaṃdhyor \\ divo mūrdhā \\ iti pratyṛcam //
18.6.d: आग्निमारुतस्तोत्रपुरस्ताद् विमोचनं परिधिषंध्योर् \\ दिवो मूर्धा \\ इति प्रत्यृचम् ॥
18.6.m: The unyoking is before the Āgnimāruta chant, at the junctions of the enclosing sticks, with: "Head of heaven...", per verse;
Some say: having yoked [it] at the introductory Atirātra, the unyoking [takes place] at the concluding one;

18.6.s: adhvarasamiṣṭayajurante \\ iṣṭo yajñas \\ iti pratyṛcam apare //
18.6.d: अध्वरसमिष्टयजुरन्ते \\ इष्टो यज्ञस् \\ इति प्रत्यृचम् अपरे ॥
18.6.m: Others say: at the end of the Samiṣṭayajus offerings of the Soma sacrifice, with: "Offered is the sacrifice...", per verse;

18.6.s: paśupuroḍāśam anv anūbandhyasya devikāhavīm̐ṣi nirvapati yajñapraiṣāṇi //
18.6.d: पशुपुरोडाशम् अन्व् अनूबन्ध्यस्य देविकाहवीम्̐षि निर्वपति यज्ञप्रैषाणि ॥
18.6.m: Following the animal cake of the anūbandhyā cow, he measures out the oblations to the Devikās, which have sacrificial calls of the primary sacrifice;
Boiled rice dishes for Anumati, Rākā, Sinīvālī, and Kuhū; a cake on twelve potsherds for Dhātṛ, offered entirely;

18.6.s: hṛdayaśūlānte sruvāhutīr juhoti yad ākūtāt \\ iti pratyṛcam aṣṭau //
18.6.d: हृदयशूलान्ते स्रुवाहुतीर् जुहोति यद् आकूतात् \\ इति प्रत्यृचम् अष्टौ ॥
18.6.m: At the end of the heart-spit [rite], he offers eight dipping-spoon oblations with: "From what intention...", per verse;

18.6.s: citro 'si \\ iti cityanāma kṛtvopatiṣṭhate ye agnayas \\ iti //
18.6.d: चित्रो ऽसि \\ इति चित्यनाम कृत्वोपतिष्ठते ये अग्नयस् \\ इति ॥
18.6.m: Naming the altar: "You are the bright one...", he reveres it with: "Which fires...";
At the end of the concluding Udavasānīyā rite, there is a curd offering to Mitra and Varuṇa, with a pair of hornless [goats] as the sacrificial gift;
The observances last for life, due to the lack of specification;
Or for a year, because of the indefiniteness of time;
If one is unable to pile the altar at a subsequent soma sacrifice, [he sets down] any one among the naturally perforated, Viśvajyotis, and seasonal bricks;
Because the altar has already attained the status of the Āhavanīya fire;

19.1.m: The Sautrāmaṇī is a Brāhmaṇa sacrifice for one desiring prosperity;
For one who has piled the fire altar, one who has performed a soma sacrifice, one over-purged by soma, and one who has vomited soma;

19.1.s: abhyādadhāmi \\ iti pratyṛcam āhavanīye tisraḥ samidho 'bhyādadhāti //
19.1.d: अभ्यादधामि \\ इति प्रत्यृचम् आहवनीये तिस्रः समिधो ऽभ्यादधाति ॥
19.1.m: With the verse beginning 'I place upon,' verse by verse, he places three kindling sticks upon the Āhavanīya fire.
Some [authorities hold] the reverse order for the pap (caru) and the animal [sacrifice].

19.1.s: antaḥpātyasthāne carmaṇi surāsomavikrayiṇaḥ sīsena śaṣpakrayas tokmānām ūrṇābhir lājānām̐ sūtraiḥ surāsomavikrayin krayyās te surāsomā ity āmantrya sarveṣu //
19.1.d: अन्तःपात्यस्थाने चर्मणि सुरासोमविक्रयिणः सीसेन शष्पक्रयस् तोक्मानाम् ऊर्णाभिर् लाजानाम्̐ सूत्रैः सुरासोमविक्रयिन् क्रय्यास् ते सुरासोमा इत्य् आमन्त्र्य सर्वेषु ॥
19.1.m: On a hide at the place of the antaḥpātya-peg, he buys young sprouting grass with lead, malted grain with wool, and parched grain with threads from a seller of surā and soma, addressing [him] in all [cases] with: 'O seller of surā and soma, is your surā and soma for sale?'

19.1.s: dakṣiṇena hṛtvā nagnahucūrṇāni kṛtvā tāṃś ca vrīhiśyāmākaudanayoḥ pṛthag ācāmau niṣicya cūrṇaiḥ sam̐sṛjya nidadhāti tan māsaram //
19.1.d: दक्षिणेन हृत्वा नग्नहुचूर्णानि कृत्वा तांश् च व्रीहिश्यामाकौदनयोः पृथग् आचामौ निषिच्य चूर्णैः सम्̐सृज्य निदधाति तन् मासरम् ॥
19.1.m: Having carried [them] to the south, he powders the yeast; having poured out separately the gruels of rice and śyāmāka grain porridge and mixed [them] with the powders, he deposits [the mixture]: that is māsara.

19.1.s: odanau cūrṇamāsaraiḥ sam̐sṛjya svādvīṃ tvā \\ am̐śunā te \\ iti trirātraṃ nidadhāti //
19.1.d: ओदनौ चूर्णमासरैः सम्̐सृज्य स्वाद्वीं त्वा \\ अम्̐शुना ते \\ इति त्रिरात्रं निदधाति ॥
19.1.m: Having mixed the two porridges with the powders and the māsara, he deposits [them] for three nights with: 'Thee, sweet...' and 'Through thy shoot...'

19.1.s: ekasyāḥ payasāpākṛtenāśvinena pariṣiñcati parīto ṣiñcatā \\ iti //
19.1.d: एकस्याः पयसापाकृतेनाश्विनेन परिषिञ्चति परीतो षिञ्चता \\ इति ॥
19.1.m: He sprinkles [the mixture] with the milk of one [cow], which was taken aside, dedicated to the Aśvins, with: 'Sprinkle around from here...'
And he scatters powders of young sprouting grass.
In the morning, [he sprinkles] with [the milk] of two [cows], dedicated to Sarasvatī.
On the last [morning, he sprinkles] with [the milk] of three [cows], dedicated to Indra.

19.2.m: He measures out the two altars as in the Varuṇapraghāsa rites.
The northern [altar is laid out] like that of the soma [sacrifice], with one-third of a prakrama turned back.
West of the two, he makes two mounds.
Tomorrow he performs [the rites] beginning with the placing of the praṇayanīya fire up to the placing of the ghee.
On the southern [altar], he performs [the rites] beginning with the wooden sword as in the Varuṇapraghāsa rites.

19.2.s: śvabhraṃ khātvā kharam apareṇa carmāvadhāya parisrutam āsicya kārotaram avadadhāti kārotarād vā carmaṇi mantraliṅgāt pūtām ādātte siñcanti pariṣiñcanti \\ iti //
