19.2.d: श्वभ्रं खात्वा खरम् अपरेण चर्मावधाय परिस्रुतम् आसिच्य कारोतरम् अवदधाति कारोतराद् वा चर्मणि मन्त्रलिङ्गात् पूताम् आदात्ते सिञ्चन्ति परिषिञ्चन्ति \\ इति ॥
19.2.m: Having dug a pit west of the mound, placed a hide [in it], and poured the liquor (parisrut), he inserts a filter-vessel; or, from the filter-vessel into the hide, according to the indication of the mantra, he takes the purified [liquor] with: 'They pour, they sprinkle around...'

19.2.s: sate punāti go'śvavālavālena punāti te parisrutam iti //
19.2.d: सते पुनाति गोऽश्ववालवालेन पुनाति ते परिस्रुतम् इति ॥
19.2.m: In a vessel, he strains [it] through a strainer of cow's hair and horse's hair, with: 'He purifies thy parisrut...'
[He uses the mantra] 'Purified by Vāyu...' in the case of one through whom soma has passed out [undigested].

19.2.s: uttarasyāṃ payo vaitase 'jāvilomapavitreṇa brahma kṣatram iti //
19.2.d: उत्तरस्यां पयो वैतसे ऽजाविलोमपवित्रेण ब्रह्म क्षत्रम् इति ॥
19.2.m: On the northern [altar], [he strains] milk into a cane vessel with a strainer of goat's and sheep's wool, with: 'The spiritual power and the royal power...'
The Brahman's following mantra is: 'O Adhvaryu, with the stones...'
He draws the cups of milk with: 'Surely indeed...'
And he scatters powders of wheat and kuvala jujube, with: 'Thou art splendor...'

19.2.s: sārasvatam audumbareṇopavākabadaracūrṇāni ca vīryam asi \\ iti //
19.2.d: सारस्वतम् औदुम्बरेणोपवाकबदरचूर्णानि च वीर्यम् असि \\ इति ॥
19.2.m: [He draws] the cup for Sarasvatī with [a cup] of udumbara wood, and [scatters powders] of upavāka and badara jujube, with: 'Thou art virility...'
[He draws] the cup for Indra with [a cup] of nyagrodha wood.
And [he scatters] powders of barley and karkandhu jujube, with: 'Thou art strength...'

19.2.s: sthālībhiḥ saurān nānā hi vām iti vyatyāsam //
19.2.d: स्थालीभिः सौरान् नाना हि वाम् इति व्यत्यासम् ॥
19.2.m: With the earthen pots, [he draws] the cups of surā alternately, with: 'Distinctly indeed for you both...'

19.2.s: surāgrahāñ chrīṇāti \\ ojo 'si \\ iti vṛkavyāghrasim̐halomabhiḥ pratimantraṃ miśraiḥ //
19.2.d: सुराग्रहाञ् छ्रीणाति \\ ओजो ऽसि \\ इति वृकव्याघ्रसिम्̐हलोमभिः प्रतिमन्त्रं मिश्रैः ॥
19.2.m: He blends the cups of surā, with: 'Thou art vigor...', with the hairs of a wolf, a tiger, and a lion mixed, mantra by mantra.

19.2.s: somo rājā \\ ity anuvākena grahānupatiṣṭhate yugapat //
19.2.d: सोमो राजा \\ इत्य् अनुवाकेन ग्रहानुपतिष्ठते युगपत् ॥
19.2.m: He attends upon the cups simultaneously with the section beginning 'King Soma...'
Or [he attends upon] the cups of milk with four [verses] and the cups of surā with the remainder.

19.2.s: dīkṣāvat pāvayato 'ntaḥpātye śyenapattrābhyām \\ yā yvāghram iti //
19.2.d: दीक्षावत् पावयतो ऽन्तःपात्ये श्येनपत्त्राभ्याम् \\ या य्वाघ्रम् इति ॥
19.2.m: Like the consecration, they purify [the sacrificer] at the antaḥpātya-peg with two falcon feathers, with: 'Which tiger...'
He makes [the sacrificer] look at the fire with: 'What he ground...'
The touching of the milk cups is with: 'You are united...'
[The touching] of the surā cups is with: 'You are separated...'

19.3.s: sārasvato meṣa aindra ṛṣabho madhye yūpo dakṣiṇottarāv aindravāyodhasayoḥ //
19.3.d: सारस्वतो मेष ऐन्द्र ऋषभो मध्ये यूपो दक्षिणोत्तराव् ऐन्द्रवायोधसयोः ॥
19.3.m: The ram for Sarasvatī, the bull for Indra; the sacrificial post is in the middle; the south and north [animals] are for Indra and the Aśvins [respectively].

19.3.s: vapāmārjanānte grahān ādāya pūrvavad anuvācanam \\ surāsomebhyo 'nubrūhi \\ iti //
19.3.d: वपामार्जनान्ते ग्रहान् आदाय पूर्ववद् अनुवाचनम् \\ सुरासोमेभ्यो ऽनुब्रूहि \\ इति ॥
19.3.m: At the end of wiping the omentum, having taken the cups, the recitation is summoned as before, with: 'Recite for the surā-somas.'

19.3.s: pālāśaiḥ saurān na mṛnmayam āhutim ānaśa iti śruter yas te \\ iti //
19.3.d: पालाशैः सौरान् न मृन्मयम् आहुतिम् आनश इति श्रुतेर् यस् ते \\ इति ॥
19.3.m: [He offers] the surā cups using palāśa cups, because of the Vedic text 'an earthen vessel does not reach the oblation', with: 'That which to thee...'

19.3.s: adhvaryuḥ pratiprasthātāgnīd yam aśvinā \\ ity āśvinaṃ bhakṣayanti dvirdvir āvartam //
19.3.d: अध्वर्युः प्रतिप्रस्थाताग्नीद् यम् अश्विना \\ इत्य् आश्विनं भक्षयन्ति द्विर्द्विर् आवर्तम् ॥
19.3.m: The Adhvaryu, the Pratiprasthātṛ, and the Agnīdh consume the cup for the Aśvins, repeating [the consumption] twice each, with: 'Which, O Aśvins...'
The Hotṛ, the Brahman, and the Maitrāvaruṇa consume the cup for Sarasvatī in the same manner as the Aśvins' [cup].
He pours whatever remnant there is of the earlier into the later [cup].

19.3.s: yad atra \\ iti saurān bhakṣayanti yathābhakṣitaṃ prācīnāvītino dakṣiṇataḥ //
19.3.d: यद् अत्र \\ इति सौरान् भक्षयन्ति यथाभक्षितं प्राचीनावीतिनो दक्षिणतः ॥
19.3.m: With [the mantra] "What here...", wearing their sacred thread over the right shoulder, to the south, they consume the liquor cups according to how they were consumed.
Or a hired man, one of a Vaiśya or a Rājanya [consumes it].

19.3.s: aṅgāreṣu vā bahiṣparidhi dakṣiṇato juhoty āśvinam uttare madhyame sārasvatam aindraṃ dakṣiṇe pitṛbhyas \\ iti pratimantram //
19.3.d: अङ्गारेषु वा बहिष्परिधि दक्षिणतो जुहोत्य् आश्विनम् उत्तरे मध्यमे सारस्वतम् ऐन्द्रं दक्षिणे पितृभ्यस् \\ इति प्रतिमन्त्रम् ॥
19.3.m: Or on the burning coals outside the enclosing sticks, to the south, he offers: the cup for the Aśvins on the northern [coal], the cup for Sarasvatī on the middle [one], the cup for Indra on the southern [one], each with its respective mantra ending with "to the fathers".
With "The fathers have eaten...", he pours around [the coals] with the washing-water.

19.3.s: kumbhīm āsajya kumbhavachatavitṛṇṇāṃ vālapavitrahiraṇyāny antardhāya navarcaṃ vācayati punantu mā \\ iti //
19.3.d: कुम्भीम् आसज्य कुम्भवछतवितृण्णां वालपवित्रहिरण्यान्य् अन्तर्धाय नवर्चं वाचयति पुनन्तु मा \\ इति ॥
19.3.m: Having hung up a jar perforated with a hundred holes like a pitcher, and having placed between [them] a hair filter and gold [pieces], he makes [him] recite the nine verses beginning "May they purify me..."
[The oblations] belong to the fathers accompanied by Soma, sitting on the sacrificial grass, and consumed by Agni.
If he is one through whom Soma has over-flowed, [the procedure is] as before.
With "Those who are equal...", the sacrificer offers.
And on the northern [fire], wearing the sacred thread over the left shoulder, with the next [verse].

19.3.s: anvārabdheṣu payo juhoti dve sṛtī iti //
19.3.d: अन्वारब्धेषु पयो जुहोति द्वे सृती इति ॥
19.3.m: While [the priests] touch him from behind, he offers milk with "Two paths..."

19.3.s: śeṣaṃ yajamāno bhakṣayati \\ idam̐ havir iti //
19.3.d: शेषं यजमानो भक्षयति \\ इदम्̐ हविर् इति ॥
19.3.m: The sacrificer consumes the remainder with "This offering..."
Together with his wife, having placed gold between, they purify themselves at the Cātvāla pit.

19.4.s: paśupuroḍāśān nirvapaty aindram̐ sāvitraṃ vāruṇaṃ daśakapālam //
19.4.d: पशुपुरोडाशान् निर्वपत्य् ऐन्द्रम्̐ सावित्रं वारुणं दशकपालम् ॥
19.4.m: He parcels out the animal cake offerings: one for Indra, one for Savitṛ, and one on ten potsherds for Varuṇa.
And an offering on one potsherd for the concluding bath.

19.4.s: āsādyainān ājyabhāgau yajaty atra sviṣṭakṛdvanaspatyoḥ praiṣadarśanāt //
19.4.d: आसाद्यैनान् आज्यभागौ यजत्य् अत्र स्विष्टकृद्वनस्पत्योः प्रैषदर्शनात् ॥
19.4.m: Having set these down, he offers the two butter portions here, because the call for the Sviṣṭakṛt and the Vanaspati is seen [here].
Or as previously stated, because the mantras are not prescribed.

19.4.s: trayastrim̐śataṃ dakṣiṇā dadāty anuśiśuṃ ca vaḍabadhenum //
19.4.d: त्रयस्त्रिम्̐शतं दक्षिणा ददात्य् अनुशिशुं च वडबधेनुम् ॥
19.4.m: He gives thirty-three [cows] as sacrificial gifts, and a mare with a foal.
The rules of the set of eleven victims apply to the groups of victims.

19.4.s: śamitranuśāsanaprabhṛti vanaspatyantaṃ kṛtvā somāsandīvad āsandīṃ jānumātrapādīṃ vedyor nidadhāti kṣatrasya yonir iti //
19.4.d: शमित्रनुशासनप्रभृति वनस्पत्यन्तं कृत्वा सोमासन्दीवद् आसन्दीं जानुमात्रपादीं वेद्योर् निदधाति क्षत्रस्य योनिर् इति ॥
19.4.m: Having performed [the rites] from the instruction to the slaughterer up to the Vanaspati offering, he places a chair with legs knee-high, like the Soma chair, between the two altars, with "The womb of the nobility..."

19.4.s: kṛṣṇājinam asyām āstṛṇāti mā tvā \\ iti //
19.4.d: कृष्णाजिनम् अस्याम् आस्तृणाति मा त्वा \\ इति ॥
19.4.m: On this he spreads a black antelope skin with "May not thee..."
On it the sacrificer sits down with "He has sat down..."

19.4.s: pādayo rukmā upāsyati rājatam̐ savye mṛtyor iti //
19.4.d: पादयो रुक्मा उपास्यति राजतम्̐ सव्ये मृत्योर् इति ॥
19.4.m: He throws down ornaments at [his] feet: a silver one at the left, with "From death..."
Some [say] a gold one on the head, with "Shine..."

19.4.s: khurair vasāgrahān dvātrim̐śataṃ juhoti sīsena \\ iti pratyṛcam //
19.4.d: खुरैर् वसाग्रहान् द्वात्रिम्̐शतं जुहोति सीसेन \\ इति प्रत्यृचम् ॥
19.4.m: With the hooves he offers thirty-two fat portions with "With lead...", verse by verse.
Having offered [them] two by two, he places the remainders in a shallow dish.

19.4.s: sarvasurabhyunmṛditam̐ śeṣair abhiṣiñcaty ā mukhād avasrāvayan pratidiśam̐ sarvatra sāvitram aśvinoḥ \ sarasvatyai \\ indrasya \\ iti pratimantram //
19.4.d: सर्वसुरभ्युन्मृदितम्̐ शेषैर् अभिषिञ्चत्य् आ मुखाद् अवस्रावयन् प्रतिदिशम्̐ सर्वत्र सावित्रम् अश्विनोः \ सरस्वत्यै \\ इन्द्रस्य \\ इति प्रतिमन्त्रम् ॥
19.4.m: He anoints [him], rubbed with all kinds of fragrant substances, with the remainders, making [them] flow down to his face, in each direction, [using] the verse to Savitṛ everywhere, each with its respective mantra: "Of the Aśvins...", "To Sarasvatī...", "Of Indra..."
Some [say], having poured the unguent into the consecration water.
He touches the sacrificer with "Who art thou?"
Being touched, he calls out with "O Suśloka..."

19.4.s: aṅgāni cālabhate yathāliṅgam \\ śiro me \\ iti pratimantram //
19.4.d: अङ्गानि चालभते यथालिङ्गम् \\ शिरो मे \\ इति प्रतिमन्त्रम् ॥
19.4.m: And he touches the limbs according to their characteristics, each with its respective mantra, beginning "My head..."
They lift him up according to the measures, as in the Śatarudriya rite.
He steps down onto the black antelope skin with "In nobility..."

19.4.s: trayastrim̐śaṃ vasāgrahaṃ gṛhṇāti yo bhūtānām iti //
19.4.d: त्रयस्त्रिम्̐शं वसाग्रहं गृह्णाति यो भूतानाम् इति ॥
19.4.m: He takes the thirty-third fat portion with "He who of beings..."
Some [say] a butter portion with [a cup of] Aśvattha wood.
